title: Cornish Beef Pasties
ingredients: 1/2 cup (2 oz. can) mushroom stems & pieces, drained
1/2 cup grated extra sharp cheddar cheese
Dash cayenne pepper & freshly ground black pepper
1/2 cup bite size shredded wheat biscuits crushed (= 1/4 cup)
instructions: Origin: British Isles
-- Filling --
(I always add garlic & a little A-1 steak sauce.)
-- Crust --
Heat oven to 400°.

Instructions: Cook onion in butter until clear. Add gd. beef. Cook thoroughly. Drain. Add remaining ingred's. Mix well. Sift together flour & seasonings. Stir in cereal crumbs. Add egg, butter & milk. Mix until smooth. Knead several times on floured board. Divide dough into 2 equal parts. Roll each very thin. Cut into 4, 6" circles. Place a heaping 1/4 cup filling on one half of ea. circle. Cut slots for steam to escape in other half. Fold dough over filling. Bring edges together & seal. Bake on cookie sheet 20 min. or until brown. Serve with sauce made by heating 1/3 cup milk & 1 can cream mushroom soup.
notes: Margin note: I actually got to taste the "real McCoy" in Cornwall, Sept./Oct. bellringing trip, '89[?]. I like my seasoning better.
Note: Good for company & can be frozen either before or after baking. Bake & thaw[?] — 400° oven, 10 min. in foil + 10 [min] unwrapped.

title: Lamb Kabobs
ingredients: 1 1/2 lbs. lean shoulder or leg o' lamb, cubed
instructions: 1. Trim all fat from lamb cubes; place in a shallow pan; pour mixture of salad dressing & water over; let stand, turning meat often, 1 hr.
2. Cook squash in boiling water to cover in med.-size saucepan 15 min. or 'til tender. Drain; halve; remove seeds; quarter ea. half; brush with marinade from lamb.

title: Lamb Rosé
ingredients: 3 lbs. breast of lamb, cut in 6-8 pieces
instructions: (serves 3 or 4)

Place meat fat side down in shallow baking pan. Add salt, pepper. Bake uncovered in 375° oven for about 1 1/2 hrs. Remove meat & pour off fat from pan. Replace meat in pan fat side up. Dissolve jelly in boiling water; add wine & parsley & pour over meat. Bake ca. 20 min. longer, basting 2 or 3 times with sauce in the pan.

title: Roast Shoulder of Lamb
instructions: seasoned meat tenderizer
(serves 6)

Make gashes in roast with sharp knife & force slivers of garlic deep into meat. Sprinkle all surfaces with seasoned meat tenderizer. Do not add salt. Pierce roast deeply with long-pronged fork. Mix thyme with crushed mint & rub well into surface of roast. Cover roast loosely & refrigerate overnight. To cook, preheat oven to 325°. Place roast on rack in open pan. Do not add water. Do not cover. Allow 25 min. to the lb. for medium lamb. Tenderizer reduces cooking time & shrinkage. About 45 min. before roast is done, place potatoes in the bottom of the roasting pan & brown, turning once. At the same time, cover the roast with the mint jelly, mixed with the sherry. This gives the roast a beautiful glaze & flavors the drippings for gravy.
Serve with: fresh fruit cup, pan roasted potatoes, biscuits & honey, peach pie.

title: Lamb Shoulder Chops
instructions: unseasoned meat tenderizer

Sprinkle chops evenly on both sides with meat tenderizer. Do not add salt. Pierce both sides with sharp fork. Let stand at room temperature 30-40 min. or cover loosely & refrigerate overnight. To cook chops, rub heavy skillet with piece of fat trimmed from lamb. When skillet is sizzling hot, pan broil chops over moderate heat 'til well browned, turning once. Allow 5-6 min. per side for golden brown crust & slightly pink center. Remove chops to heated platter. Drain fat from skillet. Add water to skillet & bring to boil. Blend in mint jelly, lemon juice & grated rind. Pour over broiled chops. (serves 4)
Serve with: creamed spinach, parsley potatoes, hot biscuits or rolls, green apple pie & sharp Cheddar cheese.

title: Osso Bucco
instructions: Mix flour, salt, pepper & oregano & coat lamb shanks. Brown garlic in oil, remove garlic, & brown floured lamb shanks. Place shanks in large casserole & add onion, celery, wine, & bouillon. Cover & place in 350° oven for 1 1/2 hrs. Remove cover during last 15 min. & baste & brown. (serves 4)
Serve with: tossed green salad, bread sticks, frenched green beans.

OR tossed chopped romaine, cucumber & sliced tiny tomato salad with parmesan cheese. Use Paul Newman's[?] dressing or Greek feta cheese dressing. Opt.: pitted olives; roasted Greek potatoes & a good Rosé wine; minted iced tea or Raki & H2O on ice.
The shank bones make great dog bones!

title: Lamb [chops with pesto fettuccine]
ingredients: 8 chops (shoulder has best flavor, but watch for gristle)

instructions: Header note: The fettuccine by itself is divine, but the flavoring from the lamb juice & drippings puts it "over the top".
freshly ground black pepper to coat chop.
Rub chops with herb flavored olive oil, rub a good coating of lemon zest, garlic purée, black pepper & 1/2 of pesto sauce. Marinate at least 4 hrs. or overnight.
Grill chops over med. heat 3 min. per side or to desired degree of doneness. Just don't overcook.

Drop fettuchine into boiling, salted water & return to boil, ca. 3 min. Drain & toss hot fettuccine with remaining pesto sauce, a little herbed olive oil, thick yogurt & mint & juice of 1 1/2 - 2 lemons.
Deglaze grilling pan with white vermouth & pour drippings over pasta. Sprinkle on pine nuts & liberal amt. Parmesan.
I like fresh green beans with lots of minced fresh dill & chopped cherry tomatoes & my veg. seasoning with this. GREAT MEAL!

title: Packaged Beef Dinner
instructions: chopped onion
cubed beef

title: Sauerbraten
title_note: note: "one of my favorites for co."
ingredients: 3 - 3 1/2 lb. beef round or rump, cut thick
instructions: Gingersnap gravy (see p. 24)

Thoroughly rub meat with 1 tsp salt & 1/2 tsp pepper; place in deep earthenware crock or pyrex bowl with all the spices & vegetables. Heat vinegar & water to boiling & pour hot over meat. Let cool. Cover bowl well & refrigerate. Let marinate at least 48 hrs., turning meat twice a day.

When ready to cook, remove meat from marinade & dry with paper towels. Melt butter in Dutch oven & sear meat. Strain marinade & pour over meat. Put on tight fitting cover. instructions: 2 pounds London broil; 3 jalapeño peppers, seeded and minced; 2 large garlic cloves, minced; 1/3 c red wine vinegar; 1/4 c soy sauce; 3 T olive oil; 3 T ground cumin; 8 eight-inch flour tortillas; shredded romaine, dressed with a little olive oil, lime juice, salt and pepper; 1 c canned black beans, drained and rinsed; Pico de Gallo.

In a plastic bag combine steak, peppers, garlic, vinegar, soy sauce, oil and cumin. Marinate overnight in refrigerator. Grill steak (about 6 to 7 minutes a side for a 1-inch-thick steak) when coals are ready (about 80 percent ashed over, no visible flame). Cut into thin slices. Warm tortillas on grill until golden, about 30 seconds a side. To serve, pile romaine on a tortilla, top with sliced steak and black beans; serve with Pico de Gallo. Makes 8 servings.

title: [Smoked/Grilled Beef Brisket] (clipping, title cut off)
instructions: 1/4 cup each: kosher salt, sugar, brown sugar, cumin, chili powder and freshly cracked black pepper; 2 tablespoons cayenne pepper; 1/2 cup paprika; 1 beef brisket, 10 to 12 pounds.
1. Combine salt, sugars, cumin, chili powder, black pepper, cayenne and paprika. Rub brisket thoroughly; set aside.
2. When fire is ready, place brisket on grill, not above any part of the fire. Close grill cover, open vent about 1/2 inch.
3. Feeding the fire periodically, cook 8 to 10 hours, or until internal temperature is 165 to 170 degrees and meat is very tender. Exterior should be very black.
4. Remove, trim excess fat and slice very thin. Serve with a sauce, if desired. Yield: 15 to 18 servings.

Combine 4 cups corn bread crumbs with 1 cup chopped celery, 1 1/4 cups chopped onions, 1 tsp salt, 3/4 - 1 tsp sage & 1/3 cup melted oleo.

title: Spicy City Chicken (clipping)
instructions: 3 pounds boneless chicken breasts and thighs; salt and freshly ground pepper to taste; 2 tablespoons vegetable oil; 1 tablespoon fresh lime juice; 6 scallions; 2 tablespoons unsalted butter; 6 shallots, diced; 6 large mushrooms, thinly sliced; 1 bunch cilantro, stems and leaves separated; 1 1/2 jalapeño peppers, chopped with seeds; 2 tablespoons ground cumin; 2 cups chicken stock or canned broth; 1 cup heavy cream; 3 egg yolks; 3 tablespoons palm sugar or brown sugar; 1/4 cup red wine vinegar.

Preheat broiler or prepare grill. Season chicken lightly with salt and pepper, since sauce will be spicy. Mix oil and lime juice and brush chicken and scallions with it. Broil or grill thighs about 12 minutes, breasts about 9 minutes, and scallions about 2 minutes per side. Always grill chicken skin-side down first.

Meanwhile, make sauce by melting butter in a medium skillet over moderate heat. Cook shallots and mushrooms until soft and golden, about 10 minutes. Add cilantro stems, jalapeño peppers and cumin, lower heat and cook 5 minutes. Add chicken stock. Turn heat to high and cook until liquid is reduced by half. Add cream and return to a boil. Remove from heat. Purée in a blender, strain and return to heat.

Whisk egg yolks, sugar and vinegar together in a small bowl. Pour one cup puréed sauce into egg mixture to temper. Then combine egg mixture and purée and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until sauce is thick and smooth.
Arrange chicken over a bed of rice and spoon sauce over all. Garnish with cilantro leaves and scallions. (NOTE: Sauce can be made in advance and reheated over a water bath.)

title_note: Chicken in White Wine Stars in Special Dinner," Nutrition Committee of the Georgia Heart Association; recipe from The American Heart Association Cookbook, David McKay Co.) — Yield: 8 servings, approx. 230 calories each
instructions: Suggested menu ("A Very Special Dinner"): Marinated Mushrooms; Chicken in White Wine and Yogurt Sauce; Wild Rice; Asparagus Par Excellence; Chef's Spinach Salad; Cherries Jubilee on Ice Milk.

4 chicken breasts, split and skinned; 4 tablespoons margarine; 3 tablespoons flour; 1/2 cup chicken bouillon; 3/4 cup low-fat yogurt; 1/4 cup white wine; 2 teaspoons grated lemon; 1 teaspoon salt; 1/2 teaspoon pepper; 1/2 cup sliced mushrooms.

Preheat oven to 350 degrees F. Melt 2 tablespoons margarine in a shallow baking pan; place chicken breasts in the pan. Bake, uncovered, about 30 minutes. Meanwhile, melt remaining margarine in a saucepan, add flour and cook briefly, stirring. Add bouillon, stirring constantly until mixture is thick and smooth. Add yogurt, wine, lemon rind, salt and pepper, stirring until blended. Remove pan from oven. Turn each chicken breast. Cover each with sliced mushrooms and pour sauce over all. Bake, uncovered, 30 minutes, or until tender. Serve garnished with a lemon twist or sprig of parsley.
Tip: Chicken without its skin is very lean meat that can be eaten frequently on a fat-controlled diet. Individual pieces of chicken may be skinned before or after cooking.

title: Country French Chicken (clipping, from "The Good Housekeeping Step-by-Step Cookbook," Hearst)
title_note: Makes 6 servings; prep 15 min; cook about 30 min
instructions: 1 1/2 pounds chicken cutlets; 3 tablespoons all-purpose flour; 1/2 teaspoon salt; 3/4 teaspoon ground black pepper; 2 tablespoons chopped fresh tarragon or 1 teaspoon dried, divided; 2 tablespoons olive oil, divided (you may need more); 1 pound assorted fresh mushrooms (white, cremini, shiitake), sliced; 1 large shallot, minced; 1 cup chicken broth; 1/4 cup dry white wine; chopped fresh tarragon or parsley (optional, garnish); cooked pasta or rice for serving.

Place chicken between 2 sheets of wax paper and pound with mallet or rolling pin to 1/8-inch thickness. On wax paper, mix flour, salt, pepper and 1 tablespoon fresh tarragon (1/2 teaspoon dried). Press chicken pieces into flour mixture to coat both sides. In 12-inch skillet, heat 1 tablespoon oil over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms and shallot and cook, stirring often, 12 to 15 minutes, until any liquid evaporates. Transfer to bowl.

In same skillet, heat remaining 1 tablespoon oil. Add half of chicken (don't overcrowd) and cook about 4 minutes per side, until golden. Transfer to platter; keep warm. Repeat with remaining chicken. (Add a little more oil if necessary and lower heat slightly if it gets too hot.)

To drippings in skillet, add broth, wine, mushroom mixture and remaining 1 tablespoon fresh or 1/2 teaspoon dried tarragon; boil 1 minute. Pour mushroom sauce over chicken; garnish with chopped tarragon, if desired. Serve over pasta or rice.

title: Sudie Lea's TACO Soup (8 servings)
instructions: Taco Seasoning (better & better for you than store bought!):
Thoroughly mix together; store in airtight glass jar up to 6 mo. 7 tsp. = 1 store pkg.

Soup: Brown 2 lb. ground beef (1/2 beef, 1/2 pork mixture) [use clarified butter for oil]. Remove to a bowl. Sauté 1 1/2 Cps. diced sweet onions to caramelized state. Return beef to iron stew pot. Thoroughly rinse 1 15.8 oz. can each of pinto beans; black beans; sm. Navy Beans; & Kidney beans and add to pot. Add 2 C frozen sweet white corn; 10 oz. can of San Manzano crushed or chopped tomatoes; 2-3 cups of Hunt's 100% natural Tomato Sauce; 1 large roasted & skinned Poblano pepper, finely chopped; 2 Tbsp fresh Cilantro, finely chopped; 2 tsp. parsley flakes; 4 tsp. Sea Salt; 1 Tbsp. minced fresh garlic; 1-2 Tbsp. finely chopped fresh green onions & 1/4 tsp. Ajowan* to de-gas the beans. Add 7 tsp. of above Taco Seasoning. Slowly simmer all together for 3 to 5 hours. A crock pot may also be used instead of my Iron soup pot.

Generously crumble Mexican Taco Chips over each serving and top with a little shredded Romaine or Butter lettuce & a scoop of thick yogurt mixed with chopped fresh avocado, jalapeño (minced), sharp grated cheddar cheese & fresh deseeded, chopped tomatoes. Serve with cornsticks or Anadama Bread.

title: Holiday Pork Roast (pasted clipping)
instructions: 1 cup dried apricot halves; 1/4 cup water; 1/4 cup dry sherry, divided; 1/2 cup chopped walnuts; 4 to 5 pound boneless pork loin roast; 2 cloves garlic, slivered; 1/4 teaspoon salt; 1 cup apricot preserves (about 1 12-ounce jar); 1 teaspoon Tabasco pepper sauce; 1/2 teaspoon dry mustard; 1/4 teaspoon ground ginger.

In a small saucepan combine apricots, water and 2 tablespoons sherry; simmer until apricots are tender, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat; stir in walnuts. Stuff pork roast by filling cavity where bone was removed with apricot-nut mixture; roll and tie securely with string. Place on a rack in a shallow roasting pan. Make slits in meat and insert slivers of garlic. Sprinkle with salt. Insert meat thermometer. Roast in a 325 degree oven until thermometer registers 170 degrees, about 20 to 25 minutes per pound. Meanwhile, combine apricot preserves, remaining 2 tablespoons sherry, Tabasco sauce, dry mustard and ginger. About 20 minutes before roast is done, brush with apricot glaze. Slice and serve with pan juices.

title: Amelia Meaux's Cajun Country Pork Soutache (pasted clipping; 1988 Philly Hall of Fame Grand Prize Winner, Main and Side Dish Category)
instructions: 1 pound lean ground pork; 1/2 cup onion, chopped; 1/4 cup celery, chopped; 1/4 cup green pepper, chopped; 1 clove garlic, minced [, or 2]; 1/2 teaspoon salt; 1/4 teaspoon ground red pepper; 1 8-ounce package cream cheese, cubed; 2 tablespoons green onion, chopped; 2 tablespoons parsley, chopped; 1 teaspoon filé powder (optional); 1 8-ounce can refrigerated crescent dinner rolls [handwritten: I prefer Puff Pastry or to make my own (Julia Child Vol. II)]; 1 egg, beaten.

In a medium-size skillet over medium heat, brown pork; drain off all fat. Add onion, celery, green pepper, garlic, salt and pepper. Cook over low heat 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add cream cheese, green onion, parsley and filé powder; stir until cream cheese is melted.

Unroll dough on lightly greased cookie sheet; firmly press perforations to seal. With floured rolling pin, roll dough to 12x10-inch rectangle. Spoon filling down center of dough, leaving 1 inch on both ends and 3 inches on both sides. Cut dough on each side of filling into 3/4-inch diagonal strips. Brush egg over dough strips. Fold ends of dough over filling. Lay dough strips alternately over filling, on the diagonal, forming a roll resembling a braid. Brush dough with remaining egg. Bake in preheated 350-degree oven 25 minutes or until golden brown.
notes: Handwritten: I usually sub. 1/2 lb. ground veal & 1/2 lb. ground round steak for pork, unless I grind a tenderloin of pork.

instructions: 6 Italian-style link sausages, sweet or hot; 1/2 pound elbow macaroni or twists; 4 green peppers, peeled and cut into strips; 2 red onions, sliced thin; 2 cups canned kidney beans, drained; 3 hard-cooked eggs, quartered; 3 tablespoons chopped Italian parsley; 1/4 cup olive oil; 3 tablespoons wine vinegar; 1 clove garlic, chopped; 1/2 teaspoon salt; freshly ground black pepper; pinch of oregano.

To cook the sausages, prick the skins with a fork, put them in a skillet with water to cover, bring to a boil, reduce the heat and poach 1 minute. Drain off the water, slice the sausage into 1/2-inch lengths, and fry over medium heat in a dry skillet until browned through. Cook and drain the pasta.

Combine the sausage, peppers, onions, macaroni, kidney beans, eggs and parsley in a bowl. In a second bowl combine the olive oil, vinegar, garlic, salt, pepper and oregano. Beat vigorously with a fork and pour the dressing over the salad, tossing gently. Let everything mature in the refrigerator for a few hours.

title: The Galloping Gourmet's Pizza
instructions: Make pizza dough, place on greased pan. Open a can of skinless tomatoes; pour over dough & mash down tomatoes. Place slices of mozzarella cheese all over tomato layer and then place sliced ripe olives over cheese; sprinkle garlic over the pizza & then add garnishes of your choice (e.g. anchovies, capers, sausage, green pepper, etc.); sprinkle oregano over whole pizza and pour 1 tbsp. olive oil over surface & then bake. Cut it into wedges with a silver cake slicer.
notes: Story: Preston loved watching (Australian) Graham Kerr on T-V. I gave him my Galloping Gourmet book when he set up housekeeping.

Place dough on cutting board, grilled side up. Sprinkle top with olive oil and garlic. Top with cheeses, tomato, arugula and ham. title: Veal Chops Italienne (Serves 6)
instructions: Served in traditional It. manner... in a spicy tomato sauce atop a bed of noodles. Veal steaks & chops, being very lean, are best when braised (browned in a sm. amt. of fat, seasoned, sm. amt. liquid added, covered tightly, & cooked slowly until tender).

Brown veal chops in lard. Place noodles in a 12x9" baking dish. Arrange chops on top of noodles. Combine onion soup, tomato sauce, water, Parm. cheese, oregano & pepper. Pour over chops. Cover tightly & bake in moderate oven (350°) 1 hr. Uncover. Combine bread crumbs, 2 tbsp Parm. cheese, parsley & garlic salt. Sprinkle over chops. Continue baking 15 min. or until lightly browned.

title: Veal Chop a L'Aiglon (recipe of Guido, chef at N.Y.'s posh L'Aiglon)
instructions: 1 6-oz. veal chop pounded to 1/8"; bread chop with egg & bread crumbs; cook over low flame in clarified butter until golden brown. Boil green noodles, strain them dry & mix in melted butter. Place chop on top of green noodles & cover with Mornay Sauce. Then sprinkle with Parmesan cheese. Broil until golden brown & serve piping hot.

Mornay Sauce: 3 oz. (ca. 6 tbsp) butter; 2 oz. (ca. 8 tbsp) flour; 1 pt. milk; 3 egg yolks. Stir flour into melted butter & cook for 10 min., stirring constantly. Add boiling milk & stir with whipper until creamy — ca. 8 min. Remove from fire, add egg yolks & stir for 4 min. Let cook over low flame for 15 min. — then add 3 oz. of whipping cream.
t_sub: recipe of Guido, chef at N.Y.'s posh L'Aiglon

title: Veal Steaks Party Style (Serves 6)
instructions: 1 cup sour cream

Cut veal into 6 pieces. Mix together egg, salt, pepper & paprika. Dip veal into egg mixture & then in crumbs. Brown in drippings. Add mushrooms including liquid, water, bouillon cube & garlic. Cover tightly & cook slowly 45 min. or until tender. Remove meat to platter. Add sour cream & capers to liquid in pan. Heat sauce thoroughly & serve over veal.

1 It. hot sausage, cut in 1/2" thick slices
1. Coat veal with flour. In hot Dutch oven, quickly brown veal; remove as browned.
instructions: 2. Add sausage & onions to pan drippings, & sauté until golden-brown. Return browned veal to oven.
3. Stir in salt, spaghetti-sauce mix, 2 C water, & tomato sauce until well blended; bring to boiling. Reduce heat, & simmer, covered, 1 hr.

title: Veal Scallopini
title_note: "Great! Serve with stone ground coarse grits." — from Jackie Vining (Methodist minister's wife, Leesville, La.) (friend of Annette Lucksinger), my friend
instructions: Make sauce by combining salt, paprika, salad oil, lemon juice, garlic, mustard, nutmeg & sugar. Beat well or shake in a bottle to combine thoroughly.

Lay veal flat in baking pan. Pour sauce over veal. Turn pieces of veal to coat with sauce. Dip veal into flour. Brown well in heated shortening in skillet. Add onion & green pepper. Add chicken bouillon to sauce & pour over veal. Cover & cook slowly until veal is tender, ca. 40 min. Brown mushrooms lightly in butter. Add mushrooms & olives to veal. Cook ca. 5 min more. Serve with sauce poured over veal.

title: Stuffed Mirliton (Chayote) ("Vegetable Pear")
instructions: Cut mirlitons in half & put into boiling salted water. Boil until tender, ca. 30 min., remove & cool. Scoop out the tender pulp, remove seeds, mash & leave the shell in a nice condition to hold stuffing.
buttered bread crumbs

title: Oyster Stew (Serves 6)
title_note: "I make this for Randy, not me. He loves it."
instructions: Oyster liquid

Heat milk on a simmer or low flame; add the crackers & oyster liquid. Melt butter in separate saucepan. Add oysters & cook until edges of oysters begin to curl, stirring constantly. Add salt & pepper, mix thoroughly & pour mixture into the hot milk. Cook 5 min. & serve.

title: Oysters Bienville (Serves 2)
instructions: Ice cream salt
Place ice cream salt in pie plate or layer cake pan. Place oysters on half shell on salt. Bake oysters in 350° oven until partially done — ca. 6-8 min.

Sauce: fry shallots in butter until brown. Add flour & heat until brown. Add chicken broth, shrimp, & mushrooms. Beat egg yolk with wine & slowly add to sauce, beating rapidly. Season to taste. Cook 10-15 min. over simmer flame, stirring constantly. Pour sauce over ea. oyster; cover with bread crumbs, paprika & grated cheese mixed. Place in oven to brown, ca. 12 min.

title: Stuffed Crabs (Serves 12)
instructions: Place crabs in boiling water (salted) 20 min. Drain, break off claws, separate shells & remove spongy fingers & stomach found under head. Pick out all meat & set aside. Clean upper shells thoroughly. Melt fat, add onion & brown. Blend in flour, add milk gradually, stirring until thickened. Add egg yolk, horseradish, parsley, salt, cayenne & blend well. Add crab meat, lemon juice & Worcestershire. Fill cleaned shells with mixture & top with bread crumbs & minced parsley. Bake in 450° oven 10 min. or until well browned.
notes: Story (pink ink, top, faded): Also my stoneware (I made) crab shells ... the scrubbed out real ones ... over the years. Patrick's dog, Connor, had his own[?] ... *

Story (purple ink): * Jubilee, when I was babysitting him. He ate 12 of the real ones I had in a bowl on the kitchen counter. Fortunately, he safely "passed" all of them (well chewed). I also taught him to go up & down the stairs. He was wonderful, as was our beloved Cinder.

title: Baked Fish (pasted clipping)
instructions: "With only a pat of margarine to moisten the fish, this recipe lets the fresh tastes of lemon and parsley accent the fish's natural flavor."
1 pound white fish fillets (such as flounder); 1 teaspoon lemon juice; 1/4 cup white wine; pat margarine; salt, if desired; pepper to taste; lemon slices; parsley, chopped fine.

Spray shallow baking dish with vegetable spray, lay fish in it and pour lemon juice and wine over. Marinate 1/2 hour. Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Lay fish skin-side down in marinade, dot with margarine and sprinkle with salt and pepper. Bake 10 minutes, or until flesh turns white and opaque. Place lemon slices on top of each serving, garnish with chopped parsley. Pour any pan juices over each serving.

title: Broiled Sea Scallops with Coriander Vinaigrette (clipping: "Sea scallops almost as good as unavailable, prized bay cousins," Pierre Franey, "60-Minute Gourmet," New York Times News Service; Augusta Herald, June 8-9, 1988)
page_label: 118 (two-page spread with pasted clippings; right page partly covered)
instructions: Sudie Lea underlined: "A critical point in cooking any kind of scallops is to sear them quickly on all sides over high heat to seal in the juices," "marinated them briefly in salt, pepper, olive oil, rosemary and hot pepper flakes," and "let almost all foods reach room temperature before grilling, barbecuing or sautéing."

16 large sea scallops, about 1 1/4 pounds; salt and freshly ground pepper to taste; 2 tablespoons olive oil; 3 sprigs fresh rosemary, chopped, or 1 tablespoon dried; 1/8 teaspoon red hot pepper flakes; coriander vinaigrette sauce.

One-half hour before broiling, sprinkle the scallops on all sides with salt and pepper and brush with a mixture of the oil, rosemary and pepper flakes. Put the scallops in a bowl and cover with plastic wrap. Do not refrigerate. When ready, preheat the broiler to high or preheat the outdoor grill. If broiling, arrange the scallops on a rack about 6 inches from the heat. Broil 2 minutes with the door partly open. Turn the scallops, continue broiling, leaving the door open. Broil about 2 minutes more. If grilling outdoors, put the scallops on a very hot grill and cover. Let cook 2 minutes. Turn the scallops, cover and continue cooking about 2 minutes. Do not overcook. Serve with vinaigrette.

Coriander Vinaigrette Sauce: 1 small red bell pepper, cored and seeded, cut into large pieces; 1/2 cup sliced white onions; 1 clove garlic, peeled; 1/2 cup fresh coriander, loosely packed; 1/2 cup olive oil; 2 tablespoons red-wine vinegar; salt and freshly ground pepper to taste. Combine all the ingredients in a blender and pulse to blend to a semi-coarse texture for a few seconds.
notes: Handwritten on clipping: "Sea scallops taste as good as bay cousins" — "No they don't, but this is good."

title: Spaghetti with Fresh Tomatoes and Basil (same clipping)
page_label: 118 (two-page spread with pasted clippings; right page partly covered)
instructions: 4 ripe plum tomatoes, about 1 pound; salt to taste; 3/4 pound spaghetti or any pasta of your choice; 2 tablespoons olive oil; 1 tablespoon butter; 1 tablespoon minced garlic; freshly ground pepper to taste; 2 tablespoons grated Parmesan cheese; 10 fresh basil leaves, coarsely chopped.

Core the tomatoes and peel them by dropping them into boiling water for about 9 or 10 seconds. Do not overcook. Drain immediately and peel with a paring knife. Cut them into 1/2-inch cubes, about 1 cup total. Bring about 10 cups of water to a boil and add salt. Add the spaghetti and cook 10 to 12 minutes or to the desired degree of doneness. Remove and reserve 1/4 cup of the cooking liquid. Drain the spaghetti. While the spaghetti is cooking, heat the oil and butter in a saucepan. Add the garlic. Cook and stir briefly. Do not brown. Add the tomatoes, salt and pepper. Cook and stir about 3 minutes. Add the spaghetti and the reserved 1/4 cup liquid. Cook and stir 1 minute. Add the cheese and basil. Mix and toss well and serve with broiled scallops.

title: S.L.'s Shrimp/Ham Jambalaya
ingredients: 2 heaping T (strained) bacon grease & 2 T flour. Make dark roux.
instructions: Add 1 whole finely chopped red onion; sauté 'til onion is soft; add 1 finely chopped green pepper, 1-2 cloves minced garlic; 2 long stalks of celery, thinly sliced; 1 C basmati rice, 1-2 tsp. seasoning mixture; add 1 1/2 C diced, cooked well-flavored ham; stir & sauté all together. Add 1 (14 oz.) can San Marzano crushed tomatoes & 1 Cup hearty chicken stock (I use my 1/2 pork & 1/2 chicken stock, a thicker, tastier stock); 2 t Worcestershire. Simmer until rice is almost done; add 1/2 C freshly chopped It. parsley & 1 lb. cleaned, raw shrimp. Cook until shrimp turn pink! Taste & correct seasoning. Voilà!

(My Creole Seasoning: 2 fresh bay leaves, 1 t salt, 1 t white pepper corns, 1 t dry Eng. mustard, 1/2 t cayenne, 2 t dried thyme, 2 t dry oregano, 1 t Gumbo filé (and Kosher salt[?]), 1 t roasted cumin seed. Grind all together.)

title: Sautéed Sea Scallops with Shallots and Tomatoes (clipping, "Cook It Light," Jeanne Jones)
ingredients: 1. Cut in half each scallop crosswise if too large. Set them aside.
instructions: 1 1/2 pounds sea scallops; 3 ripe plum tomatoes, about 1/2 pound; 2 tablespoons butter or olive oil; salt and freshly ground pepper to taste; 1/3 cup finely chopped shallots or scallions; 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice; 1/4 teaspoon Tabasco sauce; 4 tablespoons chopped fresh coriander.
2. Drop the tomatoes into boiling water for 12 seconds to loosen the skin. Remove the skins and halve them to remove the seeds. Cut the tomatoes into small cubes.
3. Melt the butter in a large non-stick skillet over high heat. Add the scallops, salt and pepper. Sauté the scallops, shaking the skillet and stirring so that they cook evenly, about 4 minutes.
4. Add the shallots, tomatoes, lemon juice, Tabasco and cook and stir over high heat for 2 minutes. Sprinkle the coriander over all and serve immediately.

title: Lemony Shrimp Salad (pasted clipping)
title_note: Serves 10 to 12 (196 calories, 10g fat, 113mg cholesterol per serving, based on 11)
page_label: 120[?] (page number hidden; loose notes and pasted clippings)
instructions: 2 pounds large shrimp, peeled and deveined; 4 cups green grapes, halved; 6 radishes, thinly sliced and cut into 1/8-inch dice; 1 cup "light" mayonnaise; 1/2 cup sour cream; 1/4 cup finely chopped fresh dill; finely grated zest of 2 lemons; 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice; salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste; radicchio or watercress, for garnish; whole sprigs of dill, for garnish.

1. Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add shrimp and cook 1 to 2 minutes or until just cooked through but not overcooked. Taste to test. Drain, run under cold water and pat dry. Place shrimp in a bowl with grapes and radishes.

2. In another bowl, mix mayonnaise, sour cream, dill, lemon zest and juice, salt and pepper. Add to shrimp mixture and toss well. Refrigerate, covered, at least 4 hours before serving for flavors to develop.
3. To serve, line a platter with radicchio leaves or watercress. Mound shrimp salad in the center and garnish with dill.

title: Spicy Cajun Shrimp (clipping: "Spicy foods gain in popularity")
ingredients: 2 dozen large shrimp or 1 pound medium shrimp, thawed, peeled and deveined.
instructions: Intro (summary): Spicy Cajun and Mexican foods are trendy; seafood is quick and easy. If the recipe looks too spicy, use half the seasoning and adjust.

Seasonings: 1 teaspoon ground cayenne pepper; 1/2 teaspoon black pepper; 1/2 teaspoon salt; 1/2 teaspoon crushed red pepper; 1/2 teaspoon dried thyme leaves, crushed; 1 teaspoon dried basil leaves, crushed; 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano leaves, crushed.

1/3 cup margarine [changed to: browned butter]; 1 1/2 teaspoons minced garlic; 1 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce; 1/4 cup beer at room temperature; 1 cup or 1 large tomato, diced coarsely; 3 cups cooked rice (optional).

Clean and devein the shrimp under cold running water. Drain well, then set aside. In a small bowl combine the seasonings. Combine the butter, garlic, Worcestershire and seasoning mix in a large skillet over high heat. When the butter is melted, add the tomato, then the shrimp. Cook 2 minutes, stirring evenly. Add the beer and cover, cook 1 minute longer. Remove from heat. Serve with crusty French bread and a fresh garden salad. May be served over rice.

title: Smoked Shrimp Spread (typed card, "from Nannie")
instructions: 3/4 pound cooked, peeled, deveined shrimp, fresh or frozen; 1 package (8 oz.) cream cheese, softened; 2 tablespoons finely chopped celery; 2 tablespoons finely chopped sweet pickle relish; 1 clove finely minced garlic; 2 teaspoons grated onion; 1 tablespoon lemon juice; 1 teaspoon horseradish; 1 teaspoon liquid smoke; 1 teaspoon dry mustard; 1/2 teaspoon salt; 1/4 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce; 1/4 teaspoon liquid hot pepper sauce; 2 tablespoons chopped parsley; assorted party breads, crackers, or raw vegetables.

Thaw frozen shrimp. Grind shrimp. Combine all ingredients except parsley and crackers. Chill for several hours. Shape shrimp mixture into desired form. Garnish with chopped parsley. Serve with bread, crackers, or vegetables.

title: Pecan Crusted Basa (Publix recipe card)
instructions: 1 cup pecan meal; 1 cup Progresso Italian bread crumbs; 1/4 cup Gold Medal flour; 1 tsp salt; 1/2 cup reduced fat milk; 1 egg; 2 Publix basa fillets (thawed); 1 tbsp Redwood Creek Chardonnay; 2 tbsp olive oil.

1. Combine pecan meal and bread crumbs in a mixing bowl. 2. In a separate bowl, mix flour and salt. 3. Whisk milk and egg in a third bowl until blended. 4. Cut basa into equal size portions. 5. Preheat sauté pan on medium high 1-2 minutes. 6. Coat each portion with the flour mixture. 7. Dip floured portion into the egg mixture (allow excess to drip back). 8. Coat with pecan mixture. 9. Add oil to pan and swirl to coat. 10. Sauté fish 2-3 minutes each side. 11. Add wine and simmer until the wine has evaporated (about 1 minute).
Suggested wine: Redwood Creek 2000 Chardonnay.

title: Skillet Flounder atop Garden Chopped Salad (clipping, "Simply Delicious")
instructions: Flounder is lean and well-suited to pan-frying, but don't overcook it. Feel free to adjust the seasonings in the flour mixture to your taste.

1/2 cup all-purpose flour; 1/2 teaspoon each sweet paprika, chili powder, ground cumin; salt and pepper, to taste; 1 head romaine lettuce; 1 cup each diced (1/4-inch) red bell pepper, carrots, peeled seedless cucumber, ripe tomatoes; 2 scallions, thinly sliced; 1 ripe avocado; 1 tablespoon fresh lime juice; 1/2 cup Lime Dressing; 4 flounder fillets (8 ounces each); 2 tablespoons unsalted butter; 2 tablespoons olive oil; 2 tablespoons snipped fresh chives.
1. Combine the flour, paprika, chili, cumin, salt and pepper in a shallow bowl; set aside.
2. Discard tough ribs and ends of lettuce leaves. Cut leaves into 1/2-inch pieces and place in a large bowl. Add diced pepper, carrots, cucumber and tomatoes, plus scallions.

3. Peel and pit the avocado; cut into 1/4-inch dice and place in a small bowl. Toss well with the lime juice to prevent discoloration. Add avocado to the other vegetables and toss with 6 tablespoons of Lime Dressing. Season with salt and pepper. Divide the salad evenly among 4 dinner plates.

4. Cut flounder fillets in half crosswise on diagonal. Dredge in reserved flour mixture, shaking off excess. Melt butter with the olive oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Cook fish, in batches, 3 minutes per side or until a dark golden brown.
5. Place 2 pieces of fish overlapping on top of each portion of salad. Drizzle the fish equally with the remaining dressing; sprinkle with the chives. Serve immediately.

Lime Dressing: 1/4 cup fresh lime juice; 1 teaspoon honey; 2 teaspoons grated lime zest; 1 teaspoon minced garlic; salt and pepper, to taste; 1/2 cup olive oil. Place all ingredients in a bowl and whisk until thick. Store, covered, in the refrigerator up to one week. Bring to room temperature before using. Yield: 3/4 cup.
t_main: Skillet Flounder atop Garden Chopped Salad

title: Christer Larsson's Poached Salmon with Dill Sauce (clipping; chef of Christer's, a Scandinavian restaurant in New York)
instructions: 1 shallot, peeled and chopped; 1/2 cup dry white wine; 1 sprig fresh thyme; 12 whole black peppercorns; 1 cup bottled clam juice; 1/2 cup heavy cream; salt and pepper, to taste; 1/2 bunch fresh dill (stems removed), chopped; 1 salmon fillet (with skin), about 3 pounds; 2 quarts water; 1/2 cup distilled vinegar; 1 carrot, peeled and chopped; 1 red onion, peeled and chopped; 1 leek (well-cleaned), chopped; 12 allspice berries; 1 tablespoon whole black peppercorns; 6 fresh dill sprigs, for garnish; 18 to 24 cooked new potatoes (with skins on), for serving.

1. Prepare the sauce: Place the shallot, wine, thyme and peppercorns in a saucepan. Bring to a boil; continue boiling until liquid is reduced to 4 tablespoons. Add clam juice and cream; return to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer slowly about 5 to 8 minutes. Strain, then season with salt and pepper. Reserve. (Add chopped dill just before serving.)

2. Cut salmon into 6 portions, leaving skin on. Place the water, vinegar, carrot, onion, leek, allspice and peppercorns in a heavy pot; bring to a boil. Add salmon. Reduce to a simmer and poach 6 to 8 minutes or until fish is done but still a little soft inside.

3. Remove salmon from liquid and divide among 6 plates. Strain the vegetables from the liquid and arrange them over the salmon. Garnish with dill sprigs. Spoon a tablespoon of sauce on each fish portion and serve immediately with new potatoes on the side.
t_main: Christer Larsson's Poached Salmon with Dill Sauce

title: Alaska Low-Fat Halibut Sauté (clipping: "Try Alaskan halibut for good taste, low fat," Tom Hoge, AP Wine and Food Writer)
instructions: Intro (summary): The writer describes Alaska's fish and game (king crab, salmon, halibut, razor clams, ptarmigan, fiddlehead ferns) from a visit to Anchorage, and offers this low-calorie halibut sauté.

1 pound halibut; 3 tablespoons oil, divided; 1 cup each thinly sliced carrots, chopped celery, sliced green onions and broccoli flowerets; 1/4 teaspoon grated ginger root; 1/4 cup chicken stock or water; 2 teaspoons cornstarch; 1 teaspoon grated lemon peel [or lime]; salt and pepper to taste; red pepper strips and toasted sesame seeds for garnish; [handwritten: lemon or lime juice].

Remove bones and skin from halibut. Cut fish into 1-inch cubes. Sauté in two tablespoons oil until barely cooked, and remove halibut from skillet. Sauté vegetables in remaining oil until crisp and tender. Return fish to skillet. Add ginger. Combine stock, cornstarch and lemon peel and add to fish mixture. Cook and stir until thickened and halibut flakes easily when fork-tested. Season with salt and pepper. Garnish with pepper and sesame seeds. Good with a chilled white wine.

title: McWhite Gumbo (story begins; continues on p. 127)
notes: STORY: No one ever made Gumbo as good as Wm. Lewis McWhite, USN, my father. He gathered the best from Mobile & Eastern Shore natives and supplemented the knowledge of cuisines from his travels, friends, chefs from around the world. While known & well touted for his culinary abilities, his cuisine was not for anyone with bland taste. I have NEVER forgotten the time he made it in a big pressure cooker. I was in the 5th or 6th grade, he'd just finished remodeling the kitchen (Mother was so proud of her glass door cabinets & windows), and he & Mother were having a dinner (Gumbo) gathering. The long table was beautifully set in the new kitchen with all the trimmings (salad, condiments, shrimp cocktails, authentic Fr. garlic bread, dessert, etc.) were done. The adults (Great aunt Blanche, Arlene (Mother's 1st cousin) & Bill (with whom I spent many weekends in Mobile); Aunt Sis & Uncle Owen; one other couple & me were all in the living room. They were having cocktails or beer & hors d'oeuvres. Suddenly there was an explosion in the kitchen & Daddy took off running in there. DISASTER!! Gumbo was dripping off the ceiling the entire length of the room and splattered all over the counters, table, chairs & floor. Everywhere! It resembled a swamp. The gauge pierced the ceiling. My Daddy laughed & my Mother was ...

title: Buttermilk Mashed Potatoes (clipping, adapted from "The Art of Low-Calorie Cooking," Sally Schneider)
instructions: 3 pounds all-purpose white potatoes, unpeeled and scrubbed, or peeled if desired; 1 tablespoon salt; 1 1/2 cups warm buttermilk; 1 teaspoon baking soda; 4 teaspoons unsalted butter; freshly ground pepper; [handwritten: opt. 1 t. chopped dill weed].

Place the potatoes and 1 teaspoon salt in a medium saucepan; add enough cool water to cover. Bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to moderate simmer until potatoes are tender when pierced with a fork, about 45 minutes. Drain, reserving a few tablespoons of the cooking liquid. Place potatoes in a large bowl and mash until fairly smooth (with some lumps remaining). Combine the buttermilk and baking soda and beat into the potatoes with a wooden spoon until thoroughly incorporated. If you prefer creamier potatoes, add the reserved cooking liquid. Stir in the butter, remaining salt and plenty of pepper to taste.
(Facing page: p. 167 clippings — see next entry.)

title: Spinach and Noodles Parmesan (clipping, microwave)
instructions: 1/2 cup chopped onion; 1 pkg. (10 oz.) frozen chopped spinach; 1 can (10 3/4 oz.) condensed cream of celery soup; 1/2 cup sour cream; 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese; 1/8 tsp. black pepper; 1/8 tsp. ground nutmeg; generous dash ground red pepper; 2 cups cooked wide egg noodles.

Place onion in 2-qt. microwave-safe casserole. Cover with lid; microwave on HIGH 3 minutes or until tender, stirring once during cooking. Add spinach. Cover; microwave on HIGH 5 minutes or until spinach is thawed, stirring twice during cooking. Stir in soup; stir in sour cream, cheese, black pepper, nutmeg and red pepper. Cover; microwave at 50 percent power 8 minutes or until hot, stirring once during cooking. Add hot noodles; toss to coat.

title: Basic Wild Rice (clipping)
ingredients: 1 cup wild rice; 4 cups water; 1 teaspoon salt.
instructions: Wash rice thoroughly. Place the wild rice, water and salt in a 3-quart saucepan and bring to a boil. Reduce heat, cover and simmer 45 to 60 minutes, or until rice has puffed and most of the liquid has been absorbed. Fluff rice with a fork and cook, uncovered, to evaporate any excess liquid. Variations: substitute beef or chicken bouillon for water, omitting salt. Substitute 1 cup white wine for 1 cup water.

title: Crunchy Pecan Wild Rice (clipping)
instructions: "This wild-rice side dish, crunchy with a lot of pecans, is a nice addition to almost any meal year round. But it's especially good when the new crop of pecans is available in the fall."
4 cups cooked wild rice, about 1 cup uncooked; 1 onion, finely chopped; 1 cup chopped pecans; 4 tablespoons (1/2 stick) butter; 1 teaspoon seasoned salt; 2 to 3 tablespoons fresh snipped parsley.

Prepare the wild rice according to basic directions. Sauté the onion and pecans in the butter in a small skillet, sprinkling the seasoned salt into this. Stir in the wild rice and cook until heated through. Adjust seasoning, if desired. Sprinkle with parsley.

title: Low Country Shrimp and Rice (clipping)
instructions: "While the traditional Low Country recipes use white rice, many of them, made with wild rice, make intriguing side dishes to add interest to many different types of dinners."

1/4 cup (1/2 stick) butter; 2 cups cooked wild rice, about 1/2 cup uncooked; 1 pound cooked shrimp, cut into 1/2-inch pieces; 1/2 cup minced water chestnuts; 2 eggs, lightly beaten; 1 to 2 tablespoons soy sauce, as desired; 1 or 2 green onions, chopped with some of the green tops.

Melt the butter in a large skillet. Add the rice, shrimp and water chestnuts. Cook, stirring frequently, until heated through. Combine the eggs with the soy sauce and add to the heated shrimp and rice mixture, stirring rapidly until eggs are set. Serve with the chopped green onion on top.

title: Lolley's Wild Rice and Sausage Casserole (clipping)
title_note: Makes about 20 3/4-cup servings or about 30 1/2-cup servings
instructions: "Mrs. William K. Meyer, Meridian, Mississippi, shared a recipe that had belonged to her mother, Mrs. William Lolley, Starkville, Mississippi, with the plea, 'Please help me adapt this for serving to a large group.' Here the recipe is increased to serve 20 to 30."

1 pound wild rice; 1/2 pound hot bulk sausage, crumbled, fried and drained; 1/2 pound fresh mushrooms, sliced; 1 large onion, chopped; 1 large green pepper, cut into 1-inch squares; 6 ribs celery, sliced diagonally; 2 10 1/2-ounce cans cream of mushroom soup, undiluted; 2 teaspoons salt.

Prepare the rice. Fry the sausage, remove meat from skillet and set aside. In fat remaining from sausage, sauté the mushrooms, onion, green pepper and celery. Combine the rice, sausage, sautéed vegetables, soup and salt, folding together thoroughly. Divide the mixture into 2 (2-quart) buttered casseroles. (This freezes well at this point.) Bake, uncovered, at 350 degrees 30 to 45 minutes, or until heated through. If casserole has been frozen, thaw completely and then uncover during last half of baking time.
t_main: Lolley's Wild Rice and Sausage Casserole

title: Wild Rice Petit Pois (clipping)
instructions: "When first you find the earliest baby green peas of spring, cook them until just done and then toss with this wild rice casserole with toasted slivered almonds. It's an excellent accompaniment to fish or lamb."

2 cups tiny green peas, cooked until just tender (about 1 1/2 to 2 pounds fresh peas); 4 cups cooked wild rice, about 1 cup uncooked; 3 tablespoons butter; 1/2 cup finely sliced almonds; 1 tablespoon grated orange rind; [handwritten: dash of cayenne or Tabasco].

Prepare the peas and the wild rice. Melt the butter in a 2-quart casserole and lightly toss the almonds in this. Bake almonds in a 325-degree oven, 10 to 15 minutes, stirring frequently, until almonds are lightly toasted. Add the peas, drained, and wild rice with orange rind to casserole and toss lightly to mix. Bake, uncovered, at 325 degrees until all ingredients are heated through.
notes: Handwritten note: I make this for Patrick who loves LeSueur Peas, with frozen or canned LeSueur. I also use equal parts of Jasmine or Basmati Rice and wild rice. Sprinkle sliced almonds & freshly grated nutmeg on top before baking.

title: Pizza Toppings

ingredients: 1 yellow & 1 red tomato, seeded & finely chopped
instructions: 2 small, young fresh zucchini; 2 small, young yellow squash (washed, leave on skin, finely grated)
A good handful of fresh basil, chopped; a little less of fresh oregano, chopped; about a 1/4 cup of fresh sage leaves, chopped; 1 bay leaf, finely chopped.

Sauté onions in a mixture of olive oil & clarified butter. When onions caramelize (just begin to turn to burnt sienna color) add zucchini, squash, garlic, sage & bay leaf. Add chopped tomatoes, basil & oregano and 1 Tbsp. raw sugar; 1/4 C dry red wine; 1 Tbsp. Hot Hungarian Paprika (or 1-2 Hot Biber Salçası or Turkish red pepper). Simmer over low heat to blend flavors. Add 1 lg. (14 lb.[?]) can San Marzano crushed tomatoes & continue to simmer until mixture thickens. Add 1/2 - 1 C freshly grated Romano cheese & simmer a little longer. Add Kosher salt (if necessary) to taste.

Let cool & set aside while making dough. Pour off excess liquid. Brush rolled-out pizza dough with a little beaten egg white so that crust will remain crisp. Sprinkle a layer of Romano & Mozzarella & then add sauce (a heavy coating). Top with meat of choice, thinly sliced green & bell peppers & top with more cheese (Mozzarella).

title: S.L.'s Pizza Dough (a quicker dough than the Peter Reinhart's[?] 1 Hr.[?])
instructions: Needed: White Lily Bread flour (it's a lighter flour); warm H2O; Dry Yeast, salt, sugar, Extra Virgin Olive Oil.

1 1/2 C warm H2O — add 1 Tablespoon of sugar; sprinkle on 1 pkg. "Rapid Rise" yeast. As soon as it proofs, add 3 1/2 - 4 C Bread flour [written over "White Lily / Martha White All Purpose"], 1 T my Za'atar spice mix, 1 tsp. Kosher salt & 1 T Extra Virgin Olive Oil. Mix together & knead approx. 10 min. Let dough rise in a greased bowl, covered with plastic wrap. (Ca. 30 min.) Turn dough onto board & knead just long enough to remove all bubbles. Divide in 2 & spread in 2 greased pizza pans. I brush slightly beaten egg white over this in order to keep dough from getting soggy. Spread on desired filling & bake at preheated 450° oven — 20-25 min. A hot oven always gives the best crust.

Toppings: For a tomato based filling, I prefer a simple Marinara sauce OR Biber Salçası (Turkish red pepper paste). Then sprinkle on whatever toppings you like, e.g. finely chopped onions; green peppers; Kalamata or Green olives; chopped spinach with lots of feta cheese; cooked, minced thick smoked bacon or Pancetta; pepperoni, chopped salami, etc. & finish off with freshly grated Romano on top.
My favorite vegetable filling → (see Pizza Toppings, next page)

title: Brunswick Stew ★
title_note: "(as close as I can get to the Dallas Co. (Orrville) delectable dish of my childhood. Mammy & Pappy always had this, Bar-b-que & a fudge cake for my summer visits.)"
instructions: Use iron pot! Stew down 2-3 lbs. chicken breasts in fresh tomatoes (12 large) (skinned & puréed in food processor). Use 3-6 pods finely chopped garlic; 1 very lg. bay leaf; 2-3 T lemon pepper (pure with no additives); 1-2 lbs. beef sirloin & 1-2 lbs. pork tenderloin; 1 bunch celery, finely chopped, leaves & all; 1/4 C finely chopped parsley & 1/3 C finely chopped fresh basil; 1 t thyme leaves; add a little H2O if necessary; 1/2 btl. low-sodium worcestershire & 1/2 btl. of A-1 sauce; juice of 1 lg. lemon & 1 T vinegar. Shred meat.

Sauté or "sweat" 2 C thinly sliced onions & 1-2 bell peppers; scrape 12 ears fresh corn; 1 lb. fresh butter beans (ca. 4 C) washed & trimmed; 1-2 C of fresh green beans, washed & trimmed. Add this to meat mixture & simmer all day. I stir this often & taste to correct seasonings. I may add a little sugar, more Tabasco & worcestershire if I think it needs it. Towards the end I will add 1 C mashed potatoes for thickening & correct seasoning, if necessary. Slow cooking is the secret to the blending of flavors. It's even better the 2nd day.

(I use white or red wine or raw apple cider vinegar to which I have added fresh garlic, basil & dill & stored in refrig.) I also "sweat" the onions in a little chicken stock with a little extra garlic. I also oil & warm the pot before adding anything. A seasoned iron pot doesn't scorch.
t_note: "(as close as I can get to the Dallas Co. (Orrville) delectable dish of my childhood. Mammy & Pappy always had this, Bar-b-que & a fudge cake for my summer visits.)"

instructions: 3. 8 eggs, beaten; 2/3 C chopped fresh dill; 2/3 C chopped fresh parsley; 4 T chopped fresh tarragon; 1 C crumbled feta cheese; 1 1/3 C finely chopped walnuts; 1 tsp. cayenne pepper; 1 tsp. dried oregano; 1-2 tsp. Jane's Crazy salt — mix together & combine with egg & zucchini mixture.

title: Triple Cheese Bread or Rolls
title_note: "Great! very light & perfect dinner rolls." — 350° oven — 1 loaf or 12 rolls (make clover leaf shapes in lg. muffin pan)
ingredients: 1/2 C (2 oz.) sharp or extra sharp Cabot cheddar, shredded
3 T (5/8 oz.) grated aged Parmesan cheese
instructions: Dissolve yeast in 1/4 C of the lukewarm H2O. Add remaining ingred. in mixer (fairly slow speed) to make a soft dough. (It will be slightly sticky.) Turn onto floured pastry cloth & knead until smooth & elastic. Place in greased bowl, cover & let rise 'til dbl., ca. 45-60 min.
Deflate dough, form into a long log & cut & roll into 36 1" balls. Place 3 to a large sized muffin cup (clover-leaf sketch). Makes 12 rolls — OR form into a 9" log & place in 9"x5" loaf pan.
Cover loosely with plastic wrap, place in refrig. overnight for an extra slow rise OR freeze & then bring to room temp & let rise 'til almost doubled. Takes 30 min. — an hour in warm room.
Bake rolls 20-25 min.; bread 30-35 min. Let bread cool in pan ca. 10 min. before removing.
notes: opt. 1 tsp. Za'atar (I like the flavor boost) (& sometimes sprinkle extra on top for color)

instructions: Preheat oven 400°.

title: 5★'s Dutch Slurry for Bread (not nec. for hard crust bread, e.g. Fr.)
instructions: Whisk together: 3/4 C rice flour; 1 Tbsp. bread flour; 3/4 tsp. instant yeast; 2 tsp. granulated sugar; 1/4 tsp. sea salt; 2 tsp. sunflower oil; & 6-8 Tbsp. water.
It should be smooth enough for brushing on tops of formed loaves, but not runny or lumpy.
I get the best texture by brushing it on right after I've formed the loaves for a final proofing.
This makes enough for 4 loaves. I store it in a glass jar in the frig. & add a little more water before using, if necessary.
This gives an enticing mottled, caramelized, slightly sweet & crunchy crust.
Alternatives for rice flour are: cornstarch; potato starch; fine cornmeal; cake flour or semolina for different tastes. I prefer rice flour (white or brown).

title: Sudie Lea's Sour-dough Oatmeal Bread
instructions: I use "starter" from pg. 229, The Bread-maker's Apprentice by Peter Reinhart. It is the best & most versatile of all the ones I've tried. The "barm" (starter) made from this seed culture has unbelievable longevity.

Sponge: 1 cup of "starter" or barm {Bring to room temperature. Don't forget to refresh starter!}; 1 cup of water (or whey); 1 1/2 cups Bread flour (I use a mixture of King Arthur and White Lily Bread flour).

I mix this together with a spoon & my hands. Spray olive oil or corn oil in a plastic bag. Put the dough in the bag & seal. Let sit overnight in a cool spot or refrigerate & bring to room temp & rising capacity.

Dough: 1 cup hot water or whey (105-115°); 1/2 cup Meyer's[?] Dry Goatmilk (or dry Buttermilk); 2 Tbsp. local honey; 1 pkg. or 2 1/4 tsp. dry yeast (I like Rapid Rise); 1 cup oatmeal (1/2 C quick & 1/2 C regular); 1 Tbsp. raw sugar; 1 tsp. each of salt & baking soda; 2 cups bread flour & 4 Tbsp. Vital Wheat Gluten.

Mix all together in mixmaster with bread dough hook & slow speed. Gradually add small amounts of the sponge. Add 1 more cup of bread flour. At this point I add 1 cup chopped toasted pecans. (continues on next page)

instructions: Heat oven to 350°. Grease & flour 2, 8" pans. Stir together flour, sugar, soda, salt & cocoa in bowl. Add shortening & 2/3 cp milk. Beat 2 min. at med. speed. Add rest of milk, eggs & vanilla. Beat 2 more min. Pour into prepared pans. Bake 35-40 min.

title: Nut-filled Cakes (Makes ca. 5 doz.)
title_note: "(My Turkish friends make something almost similar. They use hazelnuts.)"
instructions: 1. In sm. bowl, with a fork, combine 1 1/4 cps. finely-ground walnuts with 1/3 cp white corn syrup (or lt. agave syrup), 1 tsp rose water* & 1 tbsp butter, until thoroughly blended; refrigerate until ready to use. (A little fig jam may be added for more body & taste.)
2. Heat oven to 350°F. In med. bowl, with spoon, combine 2 1/4 cps flour (all-purpose), 1 1/2 tbsp sugar, 3/4 cp melted butter & 1 tbsp milk until mixture forms a ball. Then knead very well.

3. For ea. patty, pat 1/2 tsp of dough between palms of hands until ca. 1 1/2" across; lay on ungreased cookie sheet. Next top ea. half of patties with 1/2 tsp nut filling; then top ea. with a second patty, pressing edges together with a fork.
4. Bake until light golden, ca. 12-15 min. Cool, then store, tightly covered, until serving time. Then sprinkle generously with confectioners' sugar before arranging on cake plate.
* I have substituted almond flavoring.
This is also good with cashews; Brazil nuts for unusual flavor & very healthy; or pecans. Almonds are too bland.

title: Jeweled Apricot-Almond Bundt (clipping, BHG [Better Homes & Gardens], November 2016, "Holiday Baking")
title_note: handwritten: "Shirley loves & Randy eats this!" — Makes 16 servings
instructions: "I bake and freeze several leading up to the hectic holidays so I've got something on hand for brunches, afternoon teas, and hostess gifts," Genevieve says. Let cake stand at least 4 hours at room temperature to thaw before serving. Hands-on time 30 min.; total time 1 hr. 45 min., plus cooling.

1 1/4 cups white whole wheat flour; 1 1/4 cups unbleached all-purpose flour; 1 tsp. baking powder; 1/4 tsp. baking soda; 1/2 tsp. salt; 7 oz. almond paste, chopped or broken into chunks (2/3 cup packed); 1 1/2 cups sugar; 1 cup dried California (tart) apricots; 10 Tbsp. unsalted butter, softened; 5 large eggs, at room temperature; 1 tsp. pure almond extract; 1 tsp. pure lemon extract; 1 cup plain whole-milk yogurt.
1. Position a rack in the center of the oven; preheat to 325°F. Coat a 10-inch Bundt pan with nonstick baking spray.

2. Whisk whole wheat flour, 3/4 cup of the all-purpose flour, the baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a medium bowl. Pulse almond paste with sugar in a food processor until finely ground. Transfer to a mixing bowl. Combine apricots and remaining 1/2 cup all-purpose flour in the food processor; pulse until chopped.

3. Add butter to almond mixture. Beat with an electric mixer on medium-high speed until pale and fluffy. Scrape bowl. Turn speed to medium. Add eggs one at a time, beating until smooth and scraping bowl after each. Beat in extracts. Scrape bowl. Turn speed to low. Add flour mixture in thirds, alternating with the yogurt in two additions, mixing until each is incorporated before adding the next. Add apricot mixture. Mix just until evenly distributed and all traces of flour have disappeared. Transfer to prepared pan and smooth top.
4. Bake 1 1/4 hours or until a skewer inserted in domed part of cake comes out clean.
5. Cool in pan on a wire rack 10 minutes. Invert onto rack, lift off pan, and cool completely. Dust with powdered sugar before serving.
Each serving: 318 cal, 13 g fat, 79 mg chol, 156 mg sodium, 46 g carb, 2 g fiber, 6 g pro.

Apple Sauce Cream Filling: 2 egg whites; 1 envelope (1 tbsp) unflavored gelatin; 1/4 cp cold water; 1/2 cp boiling water; 2 tbsp lemon juice; 1/2 cp milk; 1 pkg. instant vanilla pudding; 1 jar (2 cps) applesauce; 2 tbsp grated lemon rind.

title: Fresh Apple Cake with Butter Pecan Glaze (pasted Pillsbury/White Lily clipping)
instructions: Pillsbury Baking Spray with Flour; 3 cups White Lily Enriched Bleached All-Purpose Flour; 2 tsps. ground cinnamon; 1 tsp. baking soda; 1/2 tsp. salt; 2 cups firmly packed brown sugar; 1 1/2 cups Crisco Pure Vegetable Oil; 3 large eggs, lightly beaten; 4 cups grated apples, about 4 large; 1 cup chopped pecans; 2 tsps. vanilla extract.
Butter Pecan Glaze: 1/4 cup butter; 1/2 cup pecan halves; 3/4 cup firmly packed brown sugar; 1/4 cup heavy cream; 1/4 cup corn syrup; 1/8 tsp. orange extract (optional).

HEAT oven to 350°F. Coat 10-inch fluted tube pan with no-stick cooking spray. COMBINE flour, cinnamon, baking soda and salt in medium bowl. Beat brown sugar, oil and eggs in large bowl. Gradually add flour mixture. Stir in apples, pecans and vanilla. Pour into prepared pan, no more than 3/4 full. BAKE 50 to 55 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean. Cool 15 minutes on wire rack before removing from pan. Finish cooling on wire rack.

For Glaze: MELT butter in small saucepan. Toast pecans in butter over medium heat, stirring constantly. Mix in brown sugar, cream and corn syrup. Bring to a rolling boil. Cook about 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Remove from heat. Blend in orange extract. COOL glaze until thickened. Drizzle over cake. Extra glaze may be spooned over individual slices, if desired.

title: Date Pudding (Mary Lou Damm, from Michigan)

title: Special Frosting
instructions: 2 cps sugar; 1 cp cream; 2 (1 oz.) sqs. unsweetened chocolate, grated.

Boil sugar, cream & chocolate together over high heat 3 min. without stirring. Reduce heat, continue cooking until syrup reaches soft ball stage. (Don't stir or frosting will be sugary.) Let cool. Beat until creamy & of spreading consistency. If frosting becomes too thick add sm. amt. of cream & beat smooth. Makes enough frosting for top & sides of 3-layer cake.
(I always use candy thermometer. I also add a pinch of instant coffee. In place of cream, I use diluted evaporated milk. Decorate top of cake with whole pecans.)

title: My Favorite Chocolate Cake
instructions: Heat oven to 350°F. Grease 3, 8" layer cake pans, line with waxed paper & regrease. Cream butter & sugar until very smooth. Add vanilla; beat. Add eggs & beat until light & fluffy. Add melted choc.; beat. * Sift dry ingredients together. Add to creamed mixture alternately with ice water. Pour into pans. Bake 30-35 min. For a glaze: use syrup from canned figs (boil the syrup to thicken) & add a little Myer's Dk. Rum & melted or clarified butter, & a good pinch of pwd. roasted ginger, pinch of freshly grated lemon zest & a squeeze of fresh lemon juice to cut any cloying sweetness & add a bright, perky note.

title: Cream Cheese Pound Cake (pasted Martha White card)

instructions: 1 1/2 cups butter or margarine, softened; 1 (8-oz.) pkg. cream cheese, softened; 3 cups sugar; 6 eggs; 1 1/2 teaspoons vanilla; 3 cups Martha White All Purpose Flour; 1/4 teaspoon salt; powdered sugar, if desired.

Heat oven to 325°F. Grease and flour bottom and sides of 10-inch tube pan or 12-cup Bundt pan. In large bowl, beat butter and cream cheese on medium speed until well mixed. Add sugar; beat until light and fluffy. Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition. Beat in vanilla. Spoon flour into measuring cup; level off. Add flour and salt. Beat just until mixed. Spoon batter into greased pan. Bake at 325°F. for 1 hour 35 minutes to 1 hour 45 minutes or until toothpick inserted 1 inch from edge comes out clean. Cool in pan 5 minutes. Turn out onto wire rack and cool completely. Sift with powdered sugar. Serve with fresh fruit, if desired. Store in refrigerator.

title: Sour Cream Apple Pudding (Serves 6)
instructions: 1 egg; 1/2 cp sugar & 1/2 tsp salt; 1 tsp soda & 1/2 cp water; 1/2 cp sour cream; 6 med. apples; 1 cp flour; 1/2 tsp cinnamon or nutmeg; 1/2 cp raisins; whipped cream; chopped nuts.

title: Candy Bar Chocolate Pie
instructions: Baked 9", cooled pie crust; 20 marshmallows; 1/2 cp milk; 6 bars (3/4 oz. ea.) almond milk choc. candy (I use 3 bars of dark choc. & 3 bars milk choc.); 1 pt. whipping cream.

Combine marshmallows & milk in saucepan. Cook over low heat, stirring occasionally, 'til marshmallows melted. Add 5 candy bars & continue heat 'til candy melts. Cool thoroughly. Beat 1 cp whip. cream & fold in choc. mixture. Spoon filling in pie shell. Chill 3-4 hrs. Whip remaining cream & spread over filling. Grate remaining candy bar & sprinkle on top of pie.

title: Mrs. Sheldon's Pecan Cookies

instructions: - Beat 1 egg white stiff, but not dry.
- Fold egg into sugar mixture with knife.
- Fold in 2 cps pecans.

notes: Story: Mrs. Elaine Sheldon was the wife of Maj. Gen'l Sheldon, commandant of Ft. Polk, La. A lovely lady, an artist (painter) who appreciated the work Mary Lou Damm, Jeanette Davidson & I put into re-structuring & implementing the program (furniture, staff, schedule & activities) for the Ft. title: Creole Casserole Bread (Yield 1 loaf)
instructions: 1 C milk; 3 T dark brown sugar; 1 T salt; 2 T butter; 1 C very warm water; 2 pkg. active yeast; 1 t. cinnamon; 1/2 t. nutmeg; 4 1/2 C flour, sifted.

title: Nannie's Time-goes-by Raisin Cake
instructions: 1 C seedless raisins; 1/2 C butter; 2 1/2 C B. sugar (packed); 3 eggs; 3 (1-oz) sq. unsweetened choc.; 2 1/2 C sifted cake flour; 1/2 tsp salt; 2 tsp soda; 1/2 C buttermilk; 2 tsp vanilla; 1 C boiling water.

Cover raisins with hot water & let stand while preparing batter. Beat butter & sugar 'til light & fluffy. Beat in 1 egg at a time. Blend in melted chocolate. Add flour with salt & soda to choc. mixture in thirds, alternating with buttermilk, beginning & ending with flour. Blend in raisins (drained) & vanilla. Stir in boiling water. Bake in 350° oven, 30-35 min. Let stand in pan 10 min. then turn on rack to cool.

title: Chocolate Butter Frosting

notes: Story (bottom): Randy went to Viet Nam, but having to live between his mother & grandmother I was in the war. At least his father & grandfather were good for Patrick (8) & Preston (4).

title: Nannie's Lane Cake
instructions: 1 C butter; 2 C sugar; 3 1/2 C sifted flour; 3 t. baking pwd; 1 C milk; 1 t. vanilla; 8 egg whites.
Cream butter, gradually adding sugar. Add sifted dry ingredients alternately with milk. Add vanilla. Fold in stiffly beaten egg whites. Bake in greased floured pans at 375° ca. 30 min.
Lane Cake Filling: 1 C sugar; 1/2 C butter; 8 egg yolks; 1 C pecans, coarsely chopped; 1 C raisins; 1 C fresh grated coconut; 4 oz. Bourbon or Brandy.

Cream sugar & well beaten egg yolks & cook in dble. boiler until thick. Add raisins which have been soaked in bourbon over-night. Add coconut & pecans & spread between cake layers. Frost with 7-min. frosting or fondant icing.

title: Sweet Potato Pudding (old family recipe
ingredients: A good dose of whiskey is always a must for any sweet potato recipe!
instructions: 2 C grated raw sweet potato; 7/8 C brown sugar; 2 eggs; 2 T molasses; 1/8 t. nutmeg; 1/2 t. salt; 1/4 C melted butter; 1 t. roasted, ground ginger + 1 t. freshly grated ginger; 1/8 t. cinnamon + 1/8 tsp. cayenne; 1/2 C milk.
Grate potatoes fine. Beat eggs. Add sugar, then molasses, butter, spices & milk. Beat well & bake in well-greased casserole at 350° until firm, or about 1 hr.
My father, Wm. Lewis McWhite, Jr., was a great (albeit messy) cook who had a heavy hand with spices, esp. hot!
notes: Note: This pudding is served as a vegetable & has texture due to grating instead of making a purée.
t_sub: old family recipe, McWhite family — Serves 6-8

title: Caramel Souffle
instructions: 2/3 C sugar for caramelizing; 2 T butter; 2 T flour; 2 eggs; 3/4 C milk; 2 T sugar; 3/4 t vanilla; salt; 1/2 pt. heavy cream.

Caramelize the sugar to light brown, pour into glass pie plate & tip it until well-coated. Melt the butter, add flour & milk, stir until thick. Remove from fire, add salt & yolks of 2 eggs. Beat well, cool slightly. Add sugar & vanilla. Fold in stiffly beaten egg whites. Turn into caramelized dish. Set in a pan of water & bake in a slow oven 35-40 min.

title: Old Virginia Spoonbread
ingredients: 1 C white cornmeal; 3 C milk, scalded; 1 T butter, melted; 1 t sugar; 1 t salt; 3 eggs.
instructions: Gradually add cornmeal to milk & cook for 5 min., stirring constantly. Cool slightly & add butter, sugar, & salt. Add beaten egg yolks & fold in stiffly beaten egg whites. Bake in greased pan in a 350° oven for ca. 45 min. Serve hot from baking dish with plenty of butter.
I never liked this in my youth, but developed a taste for it after I married & had dinner parties.

title: Cherry Cartwheels (Serves 8-10)
instructions: 2 C sifted all-purpose flour; 2 T sugar; 1/2 t salt; 1 T baking pwd; 1/3 C shortening (organic lard); 1/2 C evaporated goat milk; 1/4 C water; 1/4 C butter, melted; 1 C (1 lb.) tart red cherries, drained; 1 C croutons (Panko crumbs are good & crunchy); 1/2 C sugar; 3/4 t cinnamon; 1 t grated lemon rind.

In a med. saucepan or bowl sift together 1st 4 ingred. Cut in shortening 'til mixture resembles coarse meal. Stir in evap. milk & water just 'til blended. Turn dough out on lightly floured board. Knead 8-10 times. Roll dough into a rectangle 12x14". Brush dough with approx. 1/2 of melted butter. Sprinkle drained cherries & croutons evenly over dough. Drizzle remaining melted butter over cherry filling. Combine 1/2 C sugar, cinnamon & lemon rind. Sprinkle over cherries. Roll dough like a jelly roll, pinching edges to seal. Cut into 1" slices. Place slices cut side down on lightly greased baking sheet. Bake in preheated hot oven (425°) 'til golden brown, about 10-15 min. Remove from baking sheet immediately & cool on racks, or serve warm from oven with Cinnamon Cream Syrup.
To make croutons: Dice fresh bread & sauté in 2 T butter until lightly browned. OR use Panko crumbs for a crunching, nutty quality.

title: Cinnamon Cream Syrup (Makes 1 1/2 C)
instructions: 1/2 C light corn syrup; 1 C sugar (use raw sugar); 1/4 C water; 1 t cinnamon OR Mixed Spice; 1/2 C evap. goat milk.

Combine corn syrup, sugar, water & cinnamon in a med.-size saucepan. Bring to a full boil over med. heat, stirring constantly. Continue boiling & stirring 2 min. Remove from heat & let cool 5 min. Stir in evap. milk. Serve warm over cherry cartwheels.

title: Chocolate & Peanut Butter Cheesecake Bars (printed web recipe)
title_note: 24 bars; prep 15 min, bake 25 min, cool 1 hr
instructions: "A tasty combination of chocolate and peanut butter complemented in cheesecake bars."

2 1/2 cups graham cracker crumbs; 3/4 cup (1 1/2 sticks) butter, melted; 3/4 cup granulated sugar, divided; 1 2/3 cups (10-oz. pkg.) Nestlé Toll House Swirled Milk Chocolate & Peanut Butter Morsels, divided; 2 pkgs. (8 oz. each) cream cheese, softened; 1/4 cup all-purpose flour; 1 tablespoon vanilla extract; 4 large eggs.

PREHEAT oven to 325°F. COMBINE crumbs, butter and 1/4 cup sugar in medium bowl. Remove 1 cup mixture and reserve for topping. Press remaining mixture onto bottom of ungreased 13 x 9-inch baking pan. Sprinkle 3/4 cup morsels over crust. BEAT cream cheese, remaining sugar, flour and vanilla extract in large mixer bowl until smooth. Add eggs, one at a time, beating until smooth. Pour over crust and morsels in pan. Sprinkle with reserved crumb topping and remaining morsels. BAKE for 25 to 30 minutes or until set. Cool completely in pan on wire rack. Refrigerate until firm. Cut into bars.

title: Cranberry Pudding Pie (makes 1 9" pie)
instructions: 1 can (1 lb.) jellied cranberry sauce; 1 pkg. (3 3/4 oz.) vanilla pudding; 3 egg yolks; 1 C milk; 1 C light cream; 1 envelope unflav. gelatin; 1/4 C cold water; 3 egg whites; 3 T sugar.
Prepare pie crust & flute edges high. Prick pie crust & chill 1 hr. Bake in hot oven until shell is golden brown. Cool.

Stir cranberry sauce until smooth & spread sauce evenly over bottom of pie shell. Pour pudding mix into a saucepan; stir in egg yolks, milk & cream. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly until smooth & thick. Sprinkle gelatin over cold water & let stand 5 min. Add gelatin mixture to hot pudding & stir 'til dissolved. Cool pudding. Beat egg whites until stiff; gradually beat in sugar, 1 T at a time, until mixture is stiff & glossy. Fold 1/2 of egg whites into pudding then fold in remaining half. Spoon pudding over cranberry sauce. Swirl top with a spoon & chill until firm.

title: Cookie Jar Gingersnaps

ingredients: * Use at least 1/2 C unsalted butter & 1/4 C organic shortening.
instructions: 2 C sifted flour; 1 T toasted pwd. ginger + 1 T freshly grated ginger; 2 t baking soda; 1 t cinnamon OR mixed spice; 1/2 t salt + 1/4 tsp. cayenne; * 3/4 C shortening; 1 C sugar (coarse raw sugar); 1 egg, unbeaten; 1/4 C molasses (unsulphured).

Measure flour, ginger, baking soda, cinnamon, & salt; sift 2 onto waxed paper & return to sifter. title: Elegant Chocolate Cake
title_note: "(Mom El's favorite) (I always made it for her nearly everytime we visited in Daphne)"
instructions: 2 1/2 C cake flour; 1 t baking soda; 1 C butter; 2 1/4 C (1 lb.) firmly packed lt. brown sugar; 1 t vanilla; 3 eggs, slightly beaten; 2 sqs. unsweetened choc. {melted & cooled}; 1 C milk; (a pinch of instant coffee).

Sift flour with soda. Cream butter until softened. Add sugar gradually, creaming 'til light & fluffy (10 min.). Beat in vanilla & then add eggs, one at a time. Stir in choc. Alternately add flour & milk & beat 'til smooth. Pour batter into 3 8" layer pans, lined with wax paper. Bake 350° 30-35 min., or make 2 9" layers & bake 35 min.

Frosting: 4 sqs. unsweetened choc.; 1/2 C butter; 4 1/2 C sifted conf. sugar; 1/3 C milk; 2 unbeaten egg whites; 1 t vanilla (or rum). Mix well. Place bowl in ice water & beat with elec. mixer until right spreading consistency.

title: Sour-cream-apple pie (6-8 servings)
instructions: 9" unbaked pie shell; 1 egg; 1 C sugar; 1 C sour cream; 2 T flour; 1/2 t vanilla; 1/4 t salt; 1 lb. apples, sliced (4 C).

instructions: Gingersnap Crust.

title: Coffee Fudge Pie
instructions: Baked piecrust shell; 1 C lt. cream; 2, 4 oz. bars sweet cooking choc., broken in sm. pieces; 2 T sugar; 4 egg yolks, slightly beaten; 1 t. vanilla; 1 t. gelatin; 1/4 C cold water; 1 T instant coffee; 4 egg whites; 1/2 C sugar; 1/2 C sour cream.

Put cream, choc., sugar in 2-qt. saucepan. Stir over med. heat until choc. melts & mixture thickens. Take off heat. Stir sm. amt. of choc. mixture into egg yolks & combine in saucepan. Stir in vanilla. Cool, stirring now & then. Pour into piecrust. Chill until firm (ca. 2 hrs.). Soften gelatin in water in 1 qt. saucepan; add coffee. Stir over low heat 'til gelatin dissolves. Cool. Beat egg whites in 1 1/2 qt. bowl 'til foamy. Beat in sugar 'til stiff. Beat in gelatin mix & sour cream at low speed. Chill few min. & spoon over choc. mixture. Chill 'til firm (ca. 3 hrs.).

title: Nannie's Low-calorie Cheese Cake
instructions: 1/4 lb. butter; 1 1/4 C graham cracker crumbs; 1 (3 oz.) pkg. lemon jello (or raspberry, lime or orange); 1 (8 oz.) pkg. soft cream cheese; 1 C sugar (ultra fine-grind); 1 tall can evap. milk, chilled.

Melt butter in iron frying pan. Add g. cracker crumbs & gently toast, stirring to prevent sticking. Line bottom of 8x10" pan with half the crumbs. Add 1 C boiling water to gelatin. Refrigerate until gelatin begins to harden. Don't let it set. Add 1 C sugar to cream cheese & soften it with fork until it can be whipped with an egg beater. Evap. milk should be thoroughly chilled, preferably overnight. Whip until it is stiff like whipped cream. Fold it into cream cheese mixture, adding gelatin. Beat entire mixture until it is creamy. Pour it over the graham cracker crumbs, putting remaining g. cracker crumbs on top. Refrigerate! Can be served within an hour.
notes: Note: I submitted this to So. Living Magazine & they printed it in magazine & their cookbook.

title: Cheese Secrets
title_note: "Randy loves these & make excellent company fare" — Bake at 400° for 10-12 min. Makes 40 rolls.
instructions: 1/4 lb. Cheddar cheese; 1 pkg. active dry yeast; 1/4 C warm water; 3/4 C hot scalded milk; 1 T sugar; 3 T butter; 1 t salt; 2 1/2 to 3 C all-purp. flour; 1 T butter, melted; 1/3 C grated Parmesan cheese.

Cut cheese into 40 1/2" cubes. Soften yeast in water. Combine in mixing bowl milk, sugar, 3 T butter, & salt. Cool to lukewarm. Stir in yeast. Gradually add flour to form a stiff dough. Knead on floured surface until smooth & satiny, 4-6 min. Divide into 4 parts. Cut each into 10 pieces. Wrap dough around cheese cube. Seal edges; shape into ball. Place on greased cookie sheets. Cover. Let rise in warm place until light, 45-60 min. Bake at 400° for 10-12 min. Brush with melted butter; dip into Parmesan cheese. Best served warm.
(For dinner rolls, cut 20 1" cubes of cheese. Cut each qtr. of dough into 5 pieces. Makes 20.)

title: Decorator Frosting (clipping)
instructions: 3 egg whites; 1/2 teaspoon cream of tartar; 1 package (1 pound) sifted confectioners' sugar.

title: Persian Baklava (clipping, courtesy of Virgie Ebrahimi)
instructions: 4 C. blanched chopped almonds; 4 C. granulated sugar; 1/4 T. cardamom; 1 lb. phyllo pastry; 1 lb. sweet butter, melted; 2 C. granulated sugar; 1 C. water; 2 T. rose water.

Blanch almonds; let dry and chop finely, reserve a few for garnish. Mix almonds well in bowl with sugar and cardamom. Grease 13 x 9 x 2 pan. Put 3 layers of pastry in pan brushing each layer with butter; handle with care so pastry will not become dry. Spread almond mixture evenly on top; cover with layer of pastry. Repeat layering almonds and pastry, brushing with butter after each layer. Put 2 layers of pastry on top and brush with butter. Cut pastry in diamond shapes. Pour remaining melted butter over it evenly. Bake 350 degrees oven 35-40 minutes until golden. Boil sugar with water 20-25 minutes on medium heat. Add rose water to syrup; let stand a few minutes (may substitute 1 tablespoon lemon juice and couple cinnamon sticks boiled with sugar and water for rose water). When baklava is baked, pour sugar syrup on top; garnish with remaining almond pieces. Cool and serve.

title: Blueberry Muffins (clipping, "Wheat flour is different in muffins," Cecily Brownstone, Associated Press Food Editor)
page_label: 235 (second view, more loose clippings laid on top)
instructions: 1 cup fork-stirred all-purpose flour; 1/2 cup fork-stirred wholewheat flour; 2 teaspoons baking powder; 1/2 teaspoon salt; 1/2 cup sugar; 1 large egg; 1/2 cup milk; 1/4 cup butter, melted; 1 cup blueberries.

Stir together flours, baking powder, salt and sugar. Beat egg and milk to blend; add to flour mixture with butter; stir only until dry ingredients are moistened. Fold in blueberries. Spoon into buttered muffin-pan cups (each 1/3 cup capacity), filling them about two-thirds full. Bake in a preheated 375-degree oven until a cake tester inserted in center comes out free of batter — 25 to 30 minutes. Loosen edges and serve hot with butter.

title: Brownie Cake (Dixie Crystals recipe card)
page_label: 235 (second view, more loose clippings laid on top)
instructions: 1 cup butter or margarine, softened; 1 box (1 pound) Dixie Crystals dark brown sugar; 3 large eggs; 2 tsp. vanilla; 7 ounces unsweetened chocolate, melted and cooled; 2 cups unsifted cake flour; 1/4 tsp. salt; 2/3 tsp. baking soda; 2/3 cup sour cream; 1 cup lukewarm water. Filling and Topping: 1 pint heavy cream; 3 TBSP sugar. Garnish: semi-sweet chocolate squares for curls.

Cream butter or margarine with sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in eggs until creamy. Add vanilla and chocolate. Stir flour, salt and baking soda together. Add flour mixture to beaten mixture alternately with sour cream in three parts. Scrape bowl frequently. Slowly stir in water. Divide batter between two greased and floured 9-inch cake pans. Bake in a preheated 350° oven for 35 minutes, or until cake is done. Remove pans from oven, cool for 15 minutes and turn layers out onto racks. When completely cool, prepare filling and topping. Beat cream with sugar until stiff. Spread between and on top of layers. Pipe cream around top edge. Decorate with chocolate curls. To prepare curls, use heat of hands to warm chocolate square. Draw blade of vegetable peeler across smooth side of square. Transfer curls carefully to cake top with a toothpick.

title: Tom's Candied Citrus Peel
instructions: Remove peel from fruit with vegetable peeler or zester. Do not include the fruit's white membrane. Combine 2 C H2O + the strips of peel in 4 C measure or med. bowl. Microwave at High (100%) 4–6 min., or until water boils. Drain. Repeat process 2 more times, boiling all the peel in 2 C water each time. This procedure removes bitterness from peel. After last boiling, rinse peel thoroughly & drain on paper towels; pat dry.
Combine 1/3 C water & granulated sugar in 3 qt. casserole. Stir in peel. Microwave at High (100%) 6–8 min., or until sugar dissolves & peel is glossy & transparent, stirring every 2 min.
Remove peel with slotted spoon to rack. Cool. Sift powd. sugar over peel. Let cool completely. Store in airtight container no longer than 1 mo.
Serve as dipper for chocolate fondue or add 1 strip of peel to cup of coffee or tea.
notes: Story: (Tom Salter was my art teacher at Kennesaw St. & forever after my friend and mentor!) He died 2008.
