title: Lemon Curd Tarts in Nut Crust
title_note: clipping ("'Cuisine' recipes draw from dinner guests")
instructions: Crust: 1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted butter, softened; 1/4 cup granulated sugar; 3/4 cup finely chopped pecans; 1 egg; 1 egg yolk; 1 teaspoon salt; 2 3/4 cups all-purpose flour.
Mix butter, sugar, pecans, whole egg, egg yolk and salt with a wooden spoon until barely blended. Add flour and knead until a smooth ball forms. Wrap in plastic and chill about 4 hours.

After chilling dough, preheat oven to 350 degrees. Roll chilled dough to about 1/4-inch thickness (for one large tart pan) or divide into 8 parts and press into 8 individual tart pans, 3 inches round by 1 inch deep. The crust should be thick.
Bake empty tart shells 12 to 15 minutes, or until edges begin to brown. Set aside to cool. Meanwhile, make lemon curd.

Lemon Curd Filling: 1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted butter, melted; 2 cups granulated sugar; 4 eggs, [handwritten: a pinch of salt]; 1 scant cup fresh lemon juice; 3/4 cup finely chopped pistachio nuts for garnish.

Combine butter, sugar, eggs and lemon juice in a bowl. Place over a pot of simmering water and stir constantly and gently with a spoon or spatula, being careful not to incorporate air. Continue stirring until mixture is pale yellow and thickly coats a spoon, 7 to 10 minutes. Strain and set aside to cool at room temperature.
Remove cooled tart shells from pans and fill with lemon curd. Garnish rims with pistachio nuts and serve. Makes 8 servings.
(NOTE: Lemon Curd Tarts can be made the day before or morning of the party. Keep curds and filling separate until almost ready to serve.)
notes: Handwritten: "Meyers Lemons make the best lemon curd!"

Story: I have 2 Meyer lemon trees & 1 lime tree. The fruit takes forever to ripen, but has a superlative lemon flavor. The same holds true for the lime. Both are green, no seeds, & you have to taste to distinguish the lemon from the lime if picking or storing at the same time.

title: Pecan Pastry
ingredients: 9 tablespoons unsalted butter, frozen, cut into small pieces
instructions: Makes one 9- to 11-inch pie pastry.

Combine flour, salt, pecans and confectioners' sugar in a food processor fitted with a steel blade. Process a few seconds to blend. Add butter and process until the mixture resembles coarse meal, 5 to 10 seconds.
With the blade of the processor turning, gradually add water until dough just begins to come together. It should adhere when pinched.

Transfer dough to a floured pastry board or work surface. Press into a round shape for easy rolling. Roll out the dough large enough to fit an 11-inch flan ring placed on a baking sheet, an 11-inch tart pan with a removable bottom, or a 9-inch pie shell. Drape the dough circle over a rolling pin and fit into the pan. Press into the pan and cut off excess dough.

Place the tart pan or pie plate on a baking sheet. Press the pastry with fingers so that it adheres to the side of the pan. If using a tart pan with straight edges, raise edges of pastry 1/4 to 1/2 inch above top of pan. With your right index finger gently press forward, while at the same time a little to the left, press your left index finger in the opposing direction to make a fluting edge. Refrigerate until ready to use.

Cover and let rise in a warm place (85°), free from drafts, 40 minutes or until doubled in bulk. Bake at 350° for 50 minutes or until bread sounds hollow when tapped. Shield loosely with an aluminum foil tent during last 10 to 15 minutes of baking, if necessary. Yield: 2 loaves.

instructions: I also use this with toasted whole wheat bread crumbs for dressing. Sometimes I use sausage (cooked & well-drained) & always toasted pecans, lots of celery, onion, green pepper, parsley, fresh sage, a little apple or pear butter or applesauce, a sprinkle of chopped fresh cranberries, an egg or 2 for binding & my rich chicken stock.* I bake it covered so that it steams & then remove cover & bake until the top browns. 1/2 to 1 stick unsalted butter for sautéing the celery, onions, gr. pepper, garlic & fresh mushrooms. The dressing should be as moist as a steamed pudding with a crusty top.
*When I have access to fresh oysters, I add 8–12 small ones, chopped. Do not sauté these. Add with the chicken stock.

title: Honey Yogurt Batter Bread
title_note: ★ one of my favorites – great with nothing on it.
ingredients: 4 C White Lily unbleached bread flour
1/4 C H2O (Perrier or Gerolsteiner) (Whey is great if you have some in refrig.)
instructions: (extra nutrition: place 1 T dry milk, 1 T soya flour & 1 T wheat germ in cup before adding flour)

Combine 2 C of flour with dry yeast & salt in lg. mixer bowl (Cuisinart with bread hook). Heat: water, yogurt & butter until warm (120°F–130°F). Add to flour mixture. Add: egg & blend 2 min. on medium speed. Stir in remaining flour & walnuts & mix by hand. Place in greased crockery bowl & cover with cotton tea towel. Let rise ca. 1 hr.
Stir down batter & knead. Spread into a well-buttered 9x5x3" pan. Cover & let rise ca. 45 min.–1 hr.
Bake: in preheated 350° oven 40–45 min. Final 10–15 min. cover bread with foil if it's getting too brown.
Place a pan of hot H2O under bread rack for a crusty crust.
t_note: ★ one of my favorites – great with nothing on it.

title: Spicy Fruit
page_label: 257 (pink Woman's Day clipping lying over the page)
instructions: 3 cups mixed dried fruit, such as pitted prunes, pitted dates, apricots and figs; 1/2 cup golden raisins; 1/3 cup sugar; 3" cinnamon stick; 6 whole cloves; 1/4 teaspoon salt; 1 can (6 ounces) frozen orange-juice concentrate.

Cut mixed fruit in small pieces. Combine with next 5 ingredients and 6 cups water. Bring to boil and simmer 15 minutes. Add orange juice and mix well. Remove cinnamon stick and cloves. Serve chilled in bowls. Makes 2 quarts, or 8 servings. Note: Can be served as a sauce for vanilla or other pudding.

title: Easy Fruit Compote
page_label: 257 (pink Woman's Day clipping lying over the page)
instructions: 2 1/2 cups mixed dried fruit (prunes, golden raisins, apricots, peaches, figs, currants); 3 lemon, orange or lime slices; 2" cinnamon stick; 1/2 cup packed light-brown sugar (optional).

Pack first 3 ingredients in a widemouthed 1-quart jar. Add sugar, if desired, and cover with boiling water. Cool. Put on screw lid and let stand in cool place several days. Then refrigerate. Makes 6 servings.

title: Fig Applesauce Cake
page_label: 257 (pink Woman's Day clipping lying over the page)
instructions: 1/2 cup shortening; 1 cup sugar; 2 eggs; 1 3/4 cups all-purpose flour; 1 teaspoon salt; 1 teaspoon baking powder; 1/2 teaspoon soda; 1 teaspoon cinnamon; 1 teaspoon crushed cardamom seed; 1 cup sweetened applesauce; 1/3 cup chopped walnuts; 1 cup chopped dried figs; thin white frosting (optional).

Cream shortening. Gradually add sugar and beat until light. Add eggs and beat until fluffy. Add dry ingredients alternately with applesauce, mixing well after each addition. Stir in nuts and figs and pour into greased 9" tube pan. Bake in moderate oven (350°F.) about 45 minutes. Cool in pan 10 minutes, then turn out on rack. While still warm, spread with frosting, if desired. Cool.

title: Golden-Raisin Pie
page_label: 257 (pink Woman's Day clipping lying over the page)
instructions: Sugar; 1 tablespoon cornstarch; 1/2 teaspoon each salt, ginger and cinnamon; 1/4 teaspoon each ground cloves and nutmeg; 3 eggs, separated; 1/2 cup light corn syrup; 1 cup dairy sour cream; 1 cup golden raisins; 2 to 3 teaspoons grated orange rind; baked 8" pie shell.

In top part of small double boiler, mix 1/4 cup sugar, the cornstarch, salt and spices. Stir in egg yolks and next 4 ingredients. Cook over simmering water, stirring, 10 minutes, or until very thick. Pour into shell. Beat egg whites until foamy. Gradually add 6 tablespoons sugar and beat until stiff. Spread on hot filling, covering edges well. Bake in hot oven (400°F.) 5 minutes, or until golden brown. Cool before cutting.

title: Marvel Date Cake with Rum Frosting
page_label: 257 (pink Woman's Day clipping lying over the page)
instructions: 1/2 cup butter or margarine, softened; 3/4 cup packed brown sugar; 2 eggs; 1 3/4 cups all-purpose flour; 2 teaspoons baking powder; 1/2 teaspoon salt; 1 teaspoon cinnamon; 1/2 teaspoon nutmeg; 1/2 cup milk; 1 tablespoon dark rum; 8 ounces pitted dates, cut up; Rum Frosting.

Cream butter, add sugar and cream until light and fluffy. Add eggs one at a time, beating thoroughly after each. Mix dry ingredients and add to first mixture alternately with combined milk and rum, beating after each addition until smooth. Stir in dates. Put in 9" tube pan lined on the bottom with waxed paper and bake in moderate oven (350°F.) about 50 minutes. Cool 2 to 3 minutes, then turn out on rack and peel off paper. Cool thoroughly, then spread top and sides of cake with frosting.
Rum Frosting: Cream 2 tablespoons butter. Add 2 cups confectioners' sugar and 1 tablespoon dark rum. Gradually beat in enough cream or milk to make frosting of spreading consistency.

title: Fig Cake
ingredients: 3 eggs (1/2 t. vanilla) — add eggs, one at a time, & vanilla.
1 t. baking soda – 1 tsp. kosher salt
instructions: (Preheat oven to 350°)
— cream until lt. & fluffy.
— combine dry ingred. & add alternately with buttermilk.
1 1/2 C fig preserves with juice, chopped (spiked with rum or cognac, orange & lemon rind)
— add last.
Spoon batter into a greased & floured 10" tube pan. Bake at 350° approx. 50 min.

(I like to dust prepared pan with ground almonds & sprinkle ground almonds on top so that when cake is inverted it rests on a layer of ground almonds. This also keeps it from getting soggy if a sugar glaze is added.)
*Walnuts are tastier!
notes: Opt. 1/2 C fresh, unsweetened coconut; 1 T freshly grated ginger.

title: Pineapple-Raisin Pie
instructions: Sugar; 3 tablespoons cornstarch; 1/4 teaspoon salt; 1 can (5 3/4 ounces) pineapple spears; 1 1/2 cups dairy sour cream; 3 eggs, separated; 1 cup seedless raisins; baked 9" pie shell.

In top part of double boiler, mix 1/2 cup sugar, the cornstarch and salt. Add syrup drained from pineapple, sour cream and egg yolks. Stir, then beat with rotary beater until smooth. Put over simmering water and cook, stirring, until very thick and smooth. Remove from heat and cool slightly. Dice pineapple, add with raisins to filling and pour into shell. Beat egg whites until foamy. Gradually add 6 tablespoons sugar and beat until stiff but not dry. Pile lightly on filling, covering completely. Bake in hot oven (400°F.) 5 minutes, or until golden brown. Cool before cutting.

title: Sudie's Almond Cookies
ingredients: 2) 1/2 C ground almonds — add & beat in. [a crossed-out line above]
instructions: Oven 350°. 35–36 whole almonds.
1) 1 C butter (unsalted); 1 C sugar; 1 egg; 1 tsp. almond extract — beat together (use food processor).
3) *2 1/2 C White Lily flour; 1 t. baking pwd.; 1/2 t. baking soda; pinch of sea salt — add & beat.

Place on 2 sheets of wax paper & shape dough into 2 long batons. Chill. Cut into even slices (approx. 35–36) & roll into balls. Place on slightly greased cookie sheet. Flatten balls with palm of hand. Put a whole almond in center of each cookie. Brush each top with beaten egg yolk.
Bake approx. 15 min.
*For "sandy" texture, substitute 1/2 C almond flour OR 1/2 C rice flour for 1/2 C regular.
For a different flavor substitute walnuts chopped very fine & place whole 1/2 walnut on top & 1 tsp. walnut flavoring. OR pecans & vanilla flavoring.
notes: Story: (Members of our CCBA Ladies' Club rave over these.) I cannot resist eating a handful everytime I pass the cookie jar. I also have to share with Susanna.

title: Ghirardelli Fudge Cake
instructions: Preheat oven 350°.

Grease & lightly flour 2 9" x 1 1/2" rd. cake pans. Measure flour, sugar, cocoa, bak. pwd., bak. soda, & salt into large bowl. Mix on low for 1 min. Add butter, milk, water, eggs & vanilla to mixture. Mix on medium speed for 1 min.; scrape down bowl. Beat on high for 3 min. Pour into prepared cake pans. Bake 30–35 min. Cool in pans 5 min. Remove from pans & cool on rack.
Ice with fudge icing (use toasted pecans or almond slices in icing & sprinkled on top of cake).

title: "Chocolate Heaven" Pudding (or could be used for pie filling)
ingredients: 2 1/2 T cornstarch – pinch of sea salt
1 t pure vanilla extract – 1 T dark rum opt.
Could also fold in egg whites to make a mousse.
instructions: 1. Combine 1st 3.
2. Whisk egg yolk & whites together in another bowl. Add 1st dry mixture & whisk into a smooth paste.
3. Slowly add this mixture to the first #1 & #2, whisk until smooth.
4. Cook in dbl. boiler, whisking, until mixture boils slowly, 5–7 min.
5. Remove from heat, add butter & vanilla (& rum). Cool slightly. Pour into 4 ramekins. Cover with plastic wrap & chill.
6. Top with whipped cream OR top with beaten egg whites (2 T [sugar] & 1 T rum) & brown in 350° oven.

title: Russian Black Bread (continues on p.262)
ingredients: 2 sqs. (1 oz. ea.) unsweetened chocolate, melted [1 sq. choc.]
3 C medium rye flour [1 1/2 C rye flour]
1 pkg. (8 oz.) chopped dates [1/2 C chopped dates]
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°.

In large bowl, combine 3 C flour, yeast, caraway seed & salt. Heat water, oil, molasses, chocolate & coffee until very warm (120°–130°F). Gradually add to dry ingredients; beat 2 min. at medium speed of mixer, scraping bowl occasionally. Beat 2 min. at high speed. With spoon, stir in rye flour & enough of remaining all-purpose flour to make a soft dough. Knead on a floured surface until smooth (ca. 10 min.). Place in a greased bowl, turning to grease top. Cover; let rise until dbld. (45–60 min.). Punch down dough. Add dates. Divide dough in half, shape each into 5" diameter

title: Pistachio Chocolate Torte
title_note: clipping ("Celebrate Valentine's Day as the Romans did, with a feast," Augusta Herald / Augusta Chronicle, Feb. 5–6, 1986). Red ink in margin: "Patrick loves pistachios" [?]
ingredients: 1/4 cup finely chopped shelled natural pistachios for garnish
instructions: Combine coffee, chocolate and butter over low heat until melted; cool. Beat eggs, sugar, vanilla and salt 10 minutes on medium-high speed; gradually blend in cooled chocolate mixture. Combine flour and finely chopped pistachios; carefully fold into chocolate batter. Spread in greased and cocoa or flour-dusted 9-inch round cake pan. Bake at 350 degrees about 30 minutes or until wooden pick inserted near comes out clean. Cool 10 minutes before removing from pan. Cool completely on wire rack. Spread top and sides with Chocolate Glaze; sprinkle coarsely chopped pistachios around top edge of torte. Chill. Makes 8 to 10 servings.

Chocolate Glaze: Combine 3 tablespoons light corn syrup and 1 tablespoon butter or margarine. Bring to boil over medium-low heat; simmer 1 minute. Remove from heat and stir in 2 ounces semi-sweet chocolate, chopped, 1 tablespoon water and 1/8 teaspoon ground cinnamon. Makes 1/2 cup.
notes: Story (clipping): Legend says the early Roman version of Valentine's Day was a spring-time feast called Lupercalia. Promises made and tokens exchanged signified lasting relationships. If you were carried away by romance, that was it. Today, Valentine's Day is more fun. You can be as serious or as lighthearted as you wish. The tradition of flowers is matched by giving a treat as sweet as the heart of the Beloved.

title: Multigrain Bread
title_note: 5/30/05. Good summer bread with sunflower seeds.
ingredients: 1 C water – preferably whey (or plain soda water)

title: Cauley Square Tea Room Key Lime Pie
ingredients: 1/2 cup fresh squeezed key lime juice (approx. 8–10 limes)
instructions: Whip egg yolks and blend with condensed milk. Add key lime juice, mixing only until juice is mixed in. Do not over beat. Pour into 9 inch baked pie shell or prepared graham cracker pie crust. Chill until set (overnight is best). Top with whipped cream if you like. For a deeper filling make one and one-half times the above recipe.
notes: Handwritten: Double recipe & top with meringue. Use macadamia nuts for nut crust instead of wafers. Decorate or garnish top of pie with finely grated lime zest.

title: My Goat Cheese Cheese Cake
ingredients: pinch of sea salt & 1/4 tsp. cream of tartar
1 Meyer lemon, zested (should be 1 heaping tsp.)
3 T Wondra or cake flour (1–2 Tbs. Cointreau [?] / lemon flavoring [?])
instructions: 11 oz. mild fresh goat cheese (I esp. like the cheese I make from goat milk, kefir, & 1/2 C yogurt)

Preheat oven to 350°F (325° for convection). Prep a 9" springform pan (I prefer my oblong one). Grind together 1/2 C sliced almonds, sweet cookies & a few ginger cookies (1 1/2–2 C pr.). Mix with 4 Tbsp melted butter & spread on bottom & sides of pan. Bake 15 min., let cool before adding filling.
Combine goat cheese with sugar, lemon juice, zest & vanilla & beat until smooth. Add beaten egg yolks, 2 or 1 at a time. On low speed add flour.
In fresh bowl, beat egg whites with salt & tartar until firm. Mix 1/2 of whites into batter & fold in remaining 1/2. Spoon into pan & bake about 40 min. (until firm). Let cool.
Make lemon curd & pour all over top of cake in pan. Refrigerate overnight before unmolding.

title: Sudie Lea's Candied Pecans
instructions: Melt butter in iron skillet. Add pecans & sauté until medium brown. Keep stirring (ca. 3–5 min.). Add brown sugar & cook until lightly caramelized, ca. 3 min. longer. Stir in the Calvados & reduce until all liquid has evaporated. Season with salt & spread out on a parchment or wax paper lined cookie sheet. Bake in 350° until crisped, ca. 4–5 min.
The secret is to stir in order to avoid any burning.
notes: Note: (I love these – great on baked sweet potatoes, pie, fresh fruit or ice cream!)

title: Sudie Lea's Coconut/Macadamia Scones
ingredients: 1 C (4 oz.) unsweetened or sweetened coconut (unsulphured)
1 lg. egg beaten with 1 1/4 C unsweetened coconut milk*
1 1/2 C fresh blueberries, raspberries OR cranberries
instructions: Preheat oven 375°F. (Bake 20–25 min., drizzle with glaze after removing tray from oven.)
Milk for brushing tops of scones
Sweetened coconut for topping
Glaze: fresh orange juice (ca. 1/4 C), grated orange zest (ca. 1 T), conf.'s sugar (ca. 1 C).

Mix together DRY ingred., cut in butter. Make a well in center & pour in wet ingred. & mix with a fork. Stir in coconut, nuts & last, the berries. Knead lightly & pat into 2 rounds 1/2" thick & cut out round shapes with biscuit cutter. Bake on parchment paper.
*Use a Thai brand (thicker & creamier).
notes: Note: (To come up with this I "merged" 2 recipes from King Arthur Whole Grain Baking.)

title: Lemon Pound Cake
ingredients: 3 t. lemon zest (ca. 3 lemons) — reserve the juice for glaze
Glaze: 1 C powd. sugar (10X); 5 t. fresh lemon juice; 1–2 Tbsp. ouzo.
instructions: Oven 325°F. Butter & flour 12-C angelfood cake pan with removable bottom or a 12-C Bundt pan.
All ingred. should be organic & room temp.

Beat butter until fluffy. Gradually beat in sugar, then lemon zest, lemon extract & salt. Beat in eggs 1 at a time. Add flour in 3 additions, beating just until blended each time. Transfer batter to baking pan. Bake cake until a golden color and tester inserted near center comes out clean, ca. 1 hour. Cut around center tube and sides of cake pan to loosen cake. Remove pan sides. Cool cake completely.
Whisk together glaze ingred. until smooth. Transfer cake to plate, then drizzle glaze over cooled cake & let stand ca. 20 min.
Enjoy!

title: Double Ginger Cookies
ingredients: 2 tsp. roasted ground ginger + 1/4 tsp. gd. cloves + 1/4 tsp. allspice
2 1/2 C all-purpose flour (or Martha White or White Lily)
instructions: Preheat oven 350°. Cream butter & sugar, ginger & salt. Blend in molasses & egg. Combine flour, bak. pw'd & soda; blend into mix. Stir in minced ginger.
Chill mixture slightly for handling ease.
Form dough into 1" balls, roll in raw sugar & arrange ca. 2" apart on buttered baking sheet or parchment paper lightly spread with oil.
Bake 10 min. Let cool 2–3 min. before transferring to cooling racks. Store in airtight container.
Yield: ca. 5 doz. cookies.
notes: Note: Definitely for ginger lovers like me. Erin also loves these!

title: Page notes
instructions: Daddy was insistent on using only the best ingredients & freshest possible and he always started soups, gumbos, stews, sauces or gravies with a roux — good, strained bacon grease or butter & flour. Good, preferably home-made from shrimp shells & fish bones & mirepoix, stock is a must. I wish I had Daddy's original notes, but since I don't, I try to remember the taste of his & the things I've learned thru the years. Miss Lucille (Creole native of Mobile) & Miss Jessie (N.O. native) gave invaluable advice.

1. Boil shrimp shells in iron pot with Zatarain's seafood boil (1/2 bag); lots of celery tops; carrots; fresh bay leaves; 1 T fresh ginger; 4-6 lg. shallots; 1-2 tsp. salt; 1 cut-up lemon & 2 Tbsp. white wine vinegar. Let simmer at least 1/2 day, cool, then strain. Should have at least 2 qt. or more. Augment with bottled clam juice and chicken stock if more liquid is needed. Set aside or refrigerate until needed.

2. Slice 2 lbs. sm. sized okra in bowl. Sprinkle with pure lemon (ca. 1-2 tsp.), pepper, a little Kosher salt & freshly gd. black pepper. Thoroughly mix with ca. 2 Tbsp flour. Heat 2 to 3 Tbsp. Bacon grease in iron ... (continues on p. 128)
notes: [McWhite Gumbo story, continued] ... furious with him. I was stunned and don't remember what happened after that. I think I went with Aunt Banty to Arlene's & Bill's. I only remember it taking more than 2 weeks to clean up the mess & make repairs & I avoided my parents & the kitchen. Consequently, I won't go near a pressure cooker or have one anywhere near me.

title: Page notes
instructions: 3. Finely chop: 4 stalks celery; 1 lg. orange or red sweet pepper; 1/2 lg. green sweet pepper; 1 whole bunch of organic green onions; 1 lg. shallot & 2 cloves of garlic & mix together.

4. Heat 3-4 Tbsp. bacon grease in same iron pot used for okra. Gradually sprinkle in 3-4 Tbsp AP flour & then keep stirring until roux has attained a good, thick mush consistency and dark brown color. Remove pot off burner.
5. Dump all veggies from #3 into iron pot, return to burner & cook until veggies are soft, stirring often.
6. Add okra to above, mix all together.

7. Add 1 whole can of Hunt's unsalted, diced tomatoes. Stir all together. Add 1 whole can San Marzano crushed tomatoes. Add 1/2 cup Hunt's Tomato Ketchup; 1/2 cup Lea & Perrins Worchestershire; 1/2 cup chopped Fresh It. parsley and stir all together; simmer an hr. or 2.
8. Add 1 tsp. thyme, 1-2 bay leaves & juice of 1 lemon, preferably Meyer. Season to taste with 1 Tbsp. chipotle pepper in adobo sauce or Tabasco.

The pecans, raisins & apples should be mixed together with 1 Tbsp. flour & a pinch of salt.

After that mixture is added and completely incorporated into dough, you may add 1/2 - 1 Cup more of bread flour. It depends on the dough consistency. You want a dough that incorporates every speck of flour, leaves the sides of the mixing bowl clean & forms a smooth ball around the dough paddle. It should be a little tacky on the surface.
Place dough in a lg. greased bowl & cover with Saran wrap. Refrigerate over-night, bring to room temp. & let rise until doubled.

Dump onto lightly floured dough board & gently knead (envelope method), cut in half. Form 2 loaves & put into glass pyrex or ceramic pans that have been thoroughly greased. Cover loaves & refrigerate over-night. Let come to room temp. and rise. Spray tops of loaves with oil or melted butter, sprinkle tops with Kosher salt, make slits lengthwise center of loaves. page_label: 199 (teal ink; right edge of handwriting covered by a pasted clipping)
instructions: (Second photo of p. 199, id AF1QipOW75FS4b0XEZbRFIwHJSAgkays6Yp0CAphGbzv, shows this text with the clipping lifted.)

CLIPPING: "Purest chocolate" (newspaper sidebar, summarized) — Baker's chocolate is made from crushed roasted cocoa nibs, roughly half cocoa butter and half cocoa solids, with no sugar. Sudie Lea underlined: "the less sugar added, the darker and tangier a dessert will be." Storage: rewrap tightly and keep cool and dry up to a year; a floury "bloom" is harmless. Substitution (underlined): 3 tablespoons cocoa powder + 1 tablespoon shortening for each ounce of unsweetened chocolate. Melting tip: fat and water don't mix — a stray drop of water can stiffen melted chocolate; reliquefy with a little shortening (not butter). Handwritten: "Do NOT USE H2O with choc.!"
notes: [Sudie Lea's Sour-dough Oatmeal Bread, continued] ... from steaming pan, & bake 20 min. longer. Check with baking thermometer & remove bread from oven when the thermometer reaches 180°. Carefully remove bread from pans & let it cool on a rack so that the bottoms will not get soggy. I place cooled loaves in brown paper sacks & place in the bread box.

Ambrosia & peanut cookies. Coffee. Beaujolais (Paul Masson) with dinner.

(The roast so tender & succulent it could have passed as a sirloin tip. I coated it with horseradish & mustard & put garlic slivers throughout & cooked it very slowly in an open pan. The whole meal was better than average.)

title: November 30th '66
title_note: Thanksgiving Dinner – Joy & Ted Bole & Jeniffer & Lisa
instructions: Tomato juice cocktails – Relish tray. Roast turkey – Cornbread dressing & stuffing – Gravy – Whipped potatoes – Horseradish green beans – Cranberry sauce – Iced tea – Cranberry Nut bread. Coffee – La. sweet potato pie – peach-pecan pie.
(Everything good (including children) except bread. It was too crumbly.)
t_note: Thanksgiving Dinner – Joy & Ted Bole & Jeniffer & Lisa

title: 20 Jan. 1967
title_note: Dinner-Bridge for Judy & Mike Belson; Jan & Bob Taylor; Shirley & Bob Lowman-Berry [?]
instructions: Canadian Punch – Cashew nuts. China pepper steak – Steamed rice – Celery oriental – Cheese secrets (rolls) – Relish tray (radish roses, mother's pickles, tiny dill pickles, carrot curls & green olives) – Mandarin salad duet (gelatin ring with ambrosia).

Without a doubt one of the best dinners we've had. All the food turned out beautifully & delicious. Randy's punch was a smashing hit. The steak & rolls were the most complimented. As the punch was strong, I served icewater in Mammy's silver goblets at mealtime.
For dessert – Rum pie with a chocolate wafer crust; coffee or spiced tea. Pie was marvelous.
For prizes Randy gave cards & boot black. Bob L.B. won 1st & Bob T. last.

We had the Taylors, Davidsons, & Lorios over for dinner at different times, but I failed to write down the menus. Our tour at Ft. Polk was a good one. We met many worthwhile people & we thoroughly enjoyed the entertaining we did.
t_note: Dinner-Bridge for Judy & Mike Belson; Jan & Bob Taylor; Shirley & Bob Lowman-Berry [?]

title: April 29, 1967
instructions: Gin & tonic – salmon-cheese ball – crackers – Kosher dills. Green salad with combination cheese dressing – sole almondine with lemon-butter sauce – Eng. peas & boiled new potatoes – fresh rolls – radish roses – iced tea. Strawberry-port pie – Coffee.
Everything was delicious. I esp. was pleased with the salad dressing; Randy the fish; & the pie is a good light one for summer.
{Bill was the contractor who helped Randy & Preston to build or remodel the cottage.}

title: May 4, 1967
instructions: Hi-balls – Rusty nails – cheesewich crackers. Green salad (just crisp lettuce) with combination cheese salad dressing (always good). Pikes Peak Roast – new potatoes & Eng. peas – buttermilk biscuits & iced tea. Cheese cake.
(Good meal! Roast tasty & cheese cake very good.) Randy was pleased.

title: May 14 '67
title_note: The family had its regular Sun. cook-out again today. Our menu was improved & worth mentioning today.
instructions: Bar-b-qued fryers – I made up the sauce with lemon juice, vinegar, A-1, worchestershire, pepper, salt, sugar, garlic pwd. & onion salt & butter – delicious! Seasoned limas in butter & milk; curried fruit (Pop had 3rds & PaPa 2nds); hot rolls with onion & parmesan cheese topping; iced tea; Nannie's potato salad; Nannie's delectable applesauce spice cake with caramel nut topping; coffee. An elegant outdoor meal.
t_note: The family had its regular Sun. cook-out again today. Our menu was improved & worth mentioning today.

title: Ft. Benning, Ga.
instructions: We had LTC Clifford (Art) to dinner 3 times in July & the meals centered on meat loaf (Mama had made it up while she was here & it was the best I've ever tasted); pork chops; rib eye steaks. Toni Bisantz, who is now in V.N., also ate with us in July & we had baked chicken. Jim Stahl [?] ate with us in Aug. & we had beef Oriental.

flags.t: No year written; 1967 inferred from the entries around it.

title: Nov. 29 '68
instructions: Tomato juice cocktail (Holdens & Mrs. E. don't drink). Mixed drinks – toasted pecans – Mama's cheese & olive balls (big hit). Grillades – Cajun Rice – Piquante Beets – Emmy Lou's green bean salad with garnishes – Crackling cornbread muffins & my brandied peaches – Paul Masson Crackling Rosé. Lady Baltimore Cake – Coffee & Cognac – Assorted Mints.

{Delightful guests. Dick & Yvonne brought us a little Xmas holly bell. Both muffins & cheese balls frozen & reheated in oven before serving & turned out very good. Meat mixture also made a day ahead & warmed in oven & mixed with rice just before serving – Ed's favorite. I put on grillades (glorified round steak) in a.m. & simmered in gravy until serving time – good. Mrs. Everhart esp. liked muffins.
Randy didn't care for Cajun rice. Beets were good enough but far from one of my favorites. I suppose I was most pleased over the cake, which was superb, & my brandied peaches.
The table was lovely! I used Randy's Army-Navy cloth & napkins, Mammy's silver goblets, candlesticks & matching bowl filled with daisies & bronze mums.}

title: April 12 '69
title_note: Cocktails & Dinner: Lundquists; Luthers; Art Clifford & Jim Staats [?]
instructions: Tomato juice cocktail (Luthers don't drink). Frozen Daiquiris – Swiss Crab canapes (Mb. bk.) – Anchovy dip & assorted salted crackers. Chinese Pepper Steak – Wild Rice – Tiny English peas with salted peanuts – Cucumber Ring with carrot sticks & radishes on side – Homemade mayonnaise – Fr. bread (I made) – Crackling Rosé wine. Ambrosia and Pecan cookies – Coffee & Cognac – Chocolate mints.

Art came dressed as hippie or "flower child" & was adorable. Jim, as always, is a delightful guest & superb mixer (good conversationalist). We enjoyed the Lundquists more as the evening grew on & were pleased to get to know them better.
The Pepper steak, as always, made a hit & Col. Lundquist asked how the pecan cookies were made.

We used our Army/Navy cloth, cranberry red candles on table & sideboard & a centerpiece of red carnations & baby's breath (a delicate compliment to the silver bowl & table setting). We used Mother's silver & it was beautiful, esp. with the goblets.
Jim, Col. Lundquist & Joanne, & Art seemed to get a big kick out of Randy's Justin Wilson records. I was pleased over remembering to set an ash-tray on the dinner table for Joanne.
